3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. 7	- Expired Sitara deals cause bridgeback errors, allocation exceptions and feedback errors. Each one starts an email chain asking Daren to extend the deal or create a new one, often to cover tiny spillover volumes (0.3 to 24 dec). Volume Management then sets up a manual accounting arrangement, or parks the gas on stranger's gas.: This is the most common thread in the batch. Each case passes through 3 to 5 people (allocator → logistics → Daren → back), with deadlines tied to close. Aimee states that an accounting arrangement 'is always created every month' for meter 7266 and for the Cilco withdrawal, and Volume Management wants a deal so it doesn't have to make one every month. Possible fixes: evergreen or auto-roll rules, a tolerance for small overflow volumes, and an automatic expiry report before month end. # Leads

Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. to either pay HPLC for underages or charge HPLC for overtakes - ie. the 
difference between what our producers put in the plant and what we take from 
the plant after shrinkage.  This adjustment arrangement doesn't seem to be 
papered - it's just occurred each month for the past 5 years on a relatively 
routine basis.

properly reflecting the deal in sitara and unify.  It has been suggested that 
we try to paper the deal for posterity (the lease to TECO has 9 more years to 
run), but, in view of the forthcoming expiration of the primary term of both 
the Comstock and Oryx (Sun and/or Kerr-McGee) contracts, I'm reluctant to 
open this can of worms.  I'd like your thoughts.

input.prompt:
Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong.

TITLE: An automatic report of flow with no deal, plus rules to auto-roll deals at meters with continuing flow, to replace one-email-per-meter requests to extend expired Sitara deals

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Gas keeps flowing at a meter after its Sitara deal expires, or on days the deal doesn't cover. The volume lands on the allocation exception screen or on Strangers Gas. A volume-management allocator (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, and others) emails Daren Farmer about one meter at a time. Daren checks with the trader or contract admin and extends the deal or creates a new one. The allocator then waits for an accounting arrangement before reallocating. Often the volumes are tiny, and threads stall when the deal owner is out.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1029.eml (Jackie Young, 4/10/2000): "Here I go again...................." / "98-6373, Sitara deal #128952 expired 3/31/2000." / "4/1 .461 decatherms"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1021.eml: "I hate to be a pest but here's the deal on the above two meters:" and "Sitara deal #214948 expired 3/27/2000.  No evergreen and no new deal referenced.  This is a little premature but this meter is active   monthly and I'm thinking that it will flow for this month with no K being applied." (whitespace as in the original)
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1018.eml: "Can you see if it is o.k. to extend the deal for the rest of the month?  It has flow every day after the 1st."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/899.eml: "No new deal # referenced and no evergreen flag." and "I'm going to place 98-9676 on Strangers Gas until you hear back from Daren or Julie."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/750.eml (Aimee Lannou, meter 7266): "An accounting arrangement is always created every month." and "volume management wants to get Bammel allocated today."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1406.eml: Daren: "The deal shows evergreen, but nothing rolled to September." Julie Meyers: "This deal was not put in right."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2003.eml (Enerfin meter 980439, about 8 messages and 5 people for 9 dec and 44 dec): "please extend Deal #422516 to cover flow  of 9 dec. for 10/6/2000 and extend deal 432556 to cover flow of 44 dec." and "Volume Mgmt is trying to clear up these issues." and "please advise when you've extended the deal so that Sherlyn can create an accounting arrangement."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1458.eml: "Unfortunately, Danny Conner handles this deal and he is out this week.  Daren said to wait until he gets back next week before we do anything with it."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) A nightly or pre-close report matches meters with measured flow against active Sitara deals, so the desk sees expiring or missing coverage before the allocator finds it. (2) A deal at a meter that flows every month (for example 7266, or 6725 "active monthly") is set evergreen or rolled forward automatically unless the desk ends it, and the evergreen flag is checked against the contract term when the deal is entered (see 1406). (3) Below a small volume tolerance (for example under 50 dec for days just past a deal's end), the volume is attached to the prior deal by rule without an email request.

AFTERWARDS
The allocator clears exceptions from the report. Only true renegotiations (such as the Duke 5892 case in 1458) reach Daren. Accounting arrangements are not rebuilt for the same meter every month.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: In March–April 2000 alone the archive holds about 20 distinct requests of this kind (e.g. 872, 879, 881, 896–899, 995, 1000, 1005, 1018, 1021, 1023, 1029, 1041, 1043, 1055, 1059, 1060), and the archive is only part of the mail. Some meters recur every month (750: "always created every month"). I use a conservative 12 cases per month.
- Time per case today: about 30 minutes across all people (allocator researches the deal and writes the email ~10, Daren checks and extends or asks the trader ~10, accounting arrangement or reallocation follow-up ~10, more for chases). The rule and report remove about 20 minutes per case. Reviewing the exception report is not counted as saved.
- 12 × 20 min = 240 min = 4.0 hours a month × $85 = $340 a month (about $4,080 a year).

Note: I did not see any text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

input.description: Proposal: OPM surveys from system data
input.prompt:
Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong.

TITLE: Feed the monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) activity-driver survey from system reports, and pre-fill the monthly hours survey with last month's figures, so managers confirm exceptions instead of filling both in every month

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Every month the OPM team (James Scribner, Shari Mao, Jennifer Reside, Suzanne Nicholie) emails two surveys. (a) An Activity Driver survey to about 25 operations managers, asking for transaction counts per RC (e.g. number of deals). (b) An Hours Survey to about 45–57 managers, asking for staff hours per activity code. Responses are late and need chasers from senior managers, and managers call the process a burden. The OPM team then follows up one by one to clarify.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1244.eml (Shari Mao, Activity Survey June 2000, 26 To: recipients): "Please fill out the attached activity driver survey with June numbers for your RC" and "If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the surveyed data, please send the report to Jennifer Reside and Shari Mao.  This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1154.eml (May Activity Survey): the same offer, "This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1180.eml (Shari Mao to Daren, follow-up): "Please provide the number of Producer Services deals for the month of May (New vs. Existing)". This is a count Sitara already holds.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1188.eml (Brenda Herod, May Hours Survey): "The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your concerns on the process burdening you." The forwarded survey says "While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers." It went to about 47 managers.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml (Sept 2000, Hours Survey moved to Access, ~57 To: recipients): "If you do not have Microsoft Access, please go to the enron.itcentral.com website and complete an IT application request"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1445.eml: deadline reminder, "We are asking for a quick turn around of the completion of the survey and although it is month end, quarter end and the planning process is near completion"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1447.eml: Daren: "I had problems in getting the newest version of Access.  So, please see the attachement below". Suzanne then follows up: "One thing I still need from you is what commercial teams your group was supporting overall ?"

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) Driver quantities (deal counts, new vs. existing, physical vs. financial, etc.) are pulled each month by the OPM team from standing Sitara/Unify/CPR reports, which is the option the OPM team itself offers. Managers no longer fill in the activity survey. (2) The hours survey is pre-filled with the prior month's hours and the RC's commercial-team mapping, and the headcount comes from HR. A manager clicks "no change" or edits only the lines that moved. (3) Reminders are sent automatically only to non-responders.

AFTERWARDS
Managers spend a few minutes confirming the pre-filled hours. The activity survey disappears for most RCs. The OPM team runs one set of queries instead of chasing about 25 replies and clarifying them one by one.

ESTIMATE (counting everyone, and not counting time moved to the OPM team)
- Frequency: monthly ("every month", 1244/1154). Recipients: about 25 for the driver survey (1244: 26 names) and about 47 for the hours survey (1188 forward list; 57 in 1415).
- Driver survey: about 20 min per manager to look up counts and fill in today. Replaced by a standing query, though the OPM team spends about 1 hour a month maintaining the queries, which is netted out. 25 × 20 = 500 min, minus 60 = 440 min saved.
- Hours survey: about 20 min per manager today. Pre-filled confirm-or-edit takes about 8 min, so 12 min saved × 47 = 564 min.
- Chasing and clarification (Herod's chase, Nicholie's follow-ups): about 60 min a month saved.
- Total ≈ 1,064 min ≈ 17.7 hours/month × $85 ≈ $1,500/month (≈ $18,000/yr).

Note: I did not see any text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong.

TITLE: Feed the monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) activity-driver survey from system reports, and pre-fill the monthly hours survey with last month's figures, so managers confirm exceptions instead of filling both in every month

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Every month the OPM team (James Scribner, Shari Mao, Jennifer Reside, Suzanne Nicholie) emails two surveys. (a) An Activity Driver survey to about 25 operations managers, asking for transaction counts per RC (e.g. number of deals). (b) An Hours Survey to about 45–57 managers, asking for staff hours per activity code. Responses are late and need chasers from senior managers, and managers call the process a burden. The OPM team then follows up one by one to clarify.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1244.eml (Shari Mao, Activity Survey June 2000, 26 To: recipients): "Please fill out the attached activity driver survey with June numbers for your RC" and "If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the surveyed data, please send the report to Jennifer Reside and Shari Mao.  This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1154.eml (May Activity Survey): the same offer, "This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1180.eml (Shari Mao to Daren, follow-up): "Please provide the number of Producer Services deals for the month of May (New vs. Existing)". This is a count Sitara already holds.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1188.eml (Brenda Herod, May Hours Survey): "The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your concerns on the process burdening you." The forwarded survey says "While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers." It went to about 47 managers.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml (Sept 2000, Hours Survey moved to Access, ~57 To: recipients): "If you do not have Microsoft Access, please go to the enron.itcentral.com website and complete an IT application request"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1445.eml: deadline reminder, "We are asking for a quick turn around of the completion of the survey and although it is month end, quarter end and the planning process is near completion"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1447.eml: Daren: "I had problems in getting the newest version of Access.  So, please see the attachement below". Suzanne then follows up: "One thing I still need from you is what commercial teams your group was supporting overall ?"

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) Driver quantities (deal counts, new vs. existing, physical vs. financial, etc.) are pulled each month by the OPM team from standing Sitara/Unify/CPR reports, which is the option the OPM team itself offers. Managers no longer fill in the activity survey. (2) The hours survey is pre-filled with the prior month's hours and the RC's commercial-team mapping, and the headcount comes from HR. A manager clicks "no change" or edits only the lines that moved. (3) Reminders are sent automatically only to non-responders.

AFTERWARDS
Managers spend a few minutes confirming the pre-filled hours. The activity survey disappears for most RCs. The OPM team runs one set of queries instead of chasing about 25 replies and clarifying them one by one.

ESTIMATE (counting everyone, and not counting time moved to the OPM team)
- Frequency: monthly ("every month", 1244/1154). Recipients: about 25 for the driver survey (1244: 26 names) and about 47 for the hours survey (1188 forward list; 57 in 1415).
- Driver survey: about 20 min per manager to look up counts and fill in today. Replaced by a standing query, though the OPM team spends about 1 hour a month maintaining the queries, which is netted out. 25 × 20 = 500 min, minus 60 = 440 min saved.
- Hours survey: about 20 min per manager today. Pre-filled confirm-or-edit takes about 8 min, so 12 min saved × 47 = 564 min.
- Chasing and clarification (Herod's chase, Nicholie's follow-ups): about 60 min a month saved.
- Total ≈ 1,064 min ≈ 17.7 hours/month × $85 ≈ $1,500/month (≈ $18,000/yr).

23	hours.  The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you 
24	responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your 
25	concerns on the process burdening you.  However, there are pressures 
26	internally to provide information to Sr. Management on a more timely basis.

65	
66	Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of May, 
67	2000.
68	
69	I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
70	to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
71	in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
72	Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
73	several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
74	Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
75	observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
76	data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
77	get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with 
78	this months data collection efforts.  Please pay particular attention this 
79	month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for 
80	data quality and timeliness.
81	
82	While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers. 
83	Please return these surveys to Shari Mao by end of day Friday, June 2.  
84	
85	Please note the following changes:
86	The Nat Gas RC's will now see deal validation and transportation rate 
87	activities therefore, these surveys will be notably longer but will not 
88	necessarily take more time
89	
90	If the survey does not contain an activity that your team spends time on, 
91	PLEASE DO NOT TYPE ANY ACTIVITIES IN THE SURVEY.  Contact Jennifer Reside at 
92	#35971 to discuss how to proceed.
93	
94	If you have any questions relating to the model or this survey, or are unable 
95	to meet the survey due date, please call Jennifer Reside at #35971 (Shari is 
96	on vacation this week).
97	
98	
99

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong.

TITLE: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination (EBB/upload or fixed spreadsheet template), with a standing "same as prior day" rule so HPL only acts on changes

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each day Calpine's fuel supply desk (Ricky Archer) phones the HPL scheduler with its gas nomination, then emails the same nomination as a Word attachment ("CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc") to the HPL scheduler, cc Daren Farmer and others. Some weeks it also sends revised resends and a separate monthly nomination. The HPL scheduler reads the Word document and keys the volumes into the nomination and path. So the same nomination is handled twice, once by phone and once by email, and then keyed by hand. The recipient changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, then others), which means the distribution list has to be maintained.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1312.eml (31 Jul 2000), Subject: "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination", attachment "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc", To rlloyd, cc dfarmer, mmccoy, rcotten
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1027.eml: "As we spoke about by phone, here is the nomination, Thanks."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1099.eml (9 May 2000): "Yesterdays (10th) as we spoke of by phone."  [original line break after "by"]
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/908.eml: "Per our phone conversation."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/880.eml: "As we spoke of this morning."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/773.eml: Subject "FW: Calpine Daily Gas Nomination (REVISED)"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1245.eml: Subject "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination and Monthly (JULY) Nomination"; 1370.eml "Calpine Daily and Monthly Gas Nomination"
- Other daily copies across 2000–2001: 579, 619, 1229, 1310, 1316, 1318, 1329, 1336, 1348, 1411, 1537, 1539, 1561, 169, 184 (all farmer-d/logistics).

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Calpine submits its nomination once, through the pipeline's electronic nomination screen or a fixed-format spreadsheet that loads straight into the HPL nomination system. The phone call is dropped except on exception days. A standing rule says the nomination stays at the prior day's volumes unless Calpine submits a change, so no-change days need no HPL action. Distribution goes to a shared scheduling mailbox, not to named people who change.

AFTERWARDS
The HPL scheduler reviews an exception or upload confirmation and acts only on changed days. There's no phone call, no Word document to open and re-key, and no need to update the list when a scheduler leaves.

ESTIMATE (HPL time only; Calpine's own time not counted)
- Frequency: daily. The subject line itself is "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination", and copies run from Feb 2000 (773) to 2001 (169, 184). I count about 30 days a month, since the gas flows every day and weekend noms are sent ahead.
- Minutes today per day (HPL side): take the phone call ~5, open the Word doc, check it against the call and key it into the nom/path ~7, plus an occasional revision resend. About 12 min.
- Afterwards: about 2 min to glance at the upload or exception. Saved about 10 min a day.
- 30 × 10 = 300 min = 5 hours/month × $85 = $425/month (≈ $5,100/yr).

Note on integrity: corpus/giron-d/sent/795.eml ("Confirmed on my end. Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path.") has no Date: header and an unusual Message-ID format. I have NOT relied on it; please treat it with suspicion. I saw no text in the cited messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

{
  "name": "Requests to extend expired deals at flowing meters",
  "today": "Gas keeps flowing at a meter after its Sitara deal ends, or on days the deal does not cover. The allocator (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou) finds it on the allocation exception screen or a feedback-error list after the month, parks the gas on Strangers Gas, and emails Daren Farmer about that one meter. valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio.

"EnTelligence" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us 
to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without 
having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book.

possible.

Joe

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The quotes are real, but the mail shows the OPM team had already made most of this change, so the 1,064 minutes a month it claims to save mostly aren't there.

**What's wrong**

1. **The hours-survey pre-fill already exists.**
   - From September 2000 the hours survey moved to an Access tool (1415, 1436, 1445). Its announcement calls it "an easier and more efficient method."
   - December 2000 (2015): "There is a new report that shows your cost center's hours from the prior month."
   - January 2001 (2080): "we were unable to roll over previous months commercial teams and headcount (FTE) information … We will roll this information over beginning next month." So carrying over commercial teams and headcount was already normal practice, and only that one month was an exception.
   - The proposal's evidence for this half comes from before the Access tool: Herod's chase is from June 2000 (1188), and Daren's spreadsheet came in because he couldn't install Access (1447). The 12 minutes × 47 managers estimate is therefore against an old baseline.
   - What might still be saved is small: entering last month's hours directly instead of showing them in a report. That needs its own evidence.

2. **The activity-driver survey doesn't appear after August 2000.**
   - The last request is the July survey (1319). That message says the hours survey was paused for July and August while activities were being consolidated, and that a "shorter and easier surveying process will begin with the September survey."
   - Every "OPM Survey" after that (1415, 1436, 1445, 2015, 2080, 84) is the hours survey only.
   - So the 440 minutes a month for this half rests on work the mail doesn't show continuing. The OPM team also already offered managers the main fix, sending a standard report instead (1154, 1244).
   - The 20 minutes per manager is also too high on the evidence: Daren's May reply was a single count, which Mao accepted with "These are the only stats that we need for now" (1180, 1190).

3. **The remaining follow-up is minor.** The clarifications that keep happening (1447 in October 2000; 84 in August 2001) are about splitting activity ES002 across commercial teams. That's a different, much smaller problem: a prompt in the tool that didn't fire. It isn't what this proposal changes.

**Is it the idea or the evidence?** Mostly the idea: it proposes something largely already built. A smaller proposal could still work if new evidence supports it, so the analyst would need to find:
- requests for the activity-driver survey after August 2000;
- signs that managers still spend real time on the Access hours survey once carry-over was restored (March 2001 onward);
- or a narrow fix for the ES002 split prompt, if the follow-ups recur often enough to be worth it.

Rejection file: `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\opm-survey-prefill-reject.json`

3	  "today": "Gas keeps flowing at a meter after its Sitara deal ends, or on days the deal does not cover. The allocator (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou) finds it on the allocation exception screen or a feedback-error list after the month, parks the gas on Strangers Gas, and emails Daren Farmer about that one meter. Daren checks with the trader or contract admin and extends the deal or enters a new one; only then can accounting build an accounting arrangement and the allocator reallocate. Many volumes are tiny, the same meters come back month after month, and threads stall when the person who owns the deal is out or on another desk.",
4	  "change": "Warn the desk before month-end about deals ending at meters that still flow, and roll steady meters and tiny overflow volumes forward by rule instead of by email.",
5	  "explanation": "A list run before month-end matches meters with recent flow against Sitara deals that end that month, so Daren or the trader can extend or end each deal before the allocator finds the gap. Deals at meters that flow every month are entered as evergreen when the contract allows it, with the evergreen flag checked against the contract term at entry. Volumes under a small tolerance on days just past a deal's end attach to the prior deal by an agreed rule. Allocators then email Daren only about real renegotiations or contract questions, such as the Duke deal at meter 5892.",

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong.

TITLE: Give Confirmations a self-service, back-dated counterparty MTM report (the planned "EnTelligence" view, or a standing CPR/mini-book query by counterparty with Delta/Vol suppressed) so auditor-driven MTM valuation requests stop going to every regional risk desk

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Counterparties' auditors need third-party valuations of their derivative positions with Enron. Confirmations (Larry Joe Hunter, Ellen Wallumrod) has no valuation system access, so each request is emailed to 5–6 regional risk desk heads (Gossett, Keiser, Love, Giron, McLaughlin, Baumbach). Each desk head forwards it to a staff member, who runs a mini-book for that counterparty as of a past date, exports it to Excel, blacks out Delta/Vol, and sends it back. Confirmations then consolidates the regional totals. Requests come several times a week and are often late.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/241.eml (Larry Joe Hunter, "Audit Request procedure", 2/8/2001): "Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio." / "please let these persons know that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several per week)." / "We do not have access to any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line \"EnTelligence\" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book." Giron's reply: "Call Pat Ryder for West desk requests."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/240.eml (CoEnergy, to 5 desk heads, forwarded by Giron to Patrick Ryder): "Please forward to Ellen Wallumrod the MTM valuation(mini-book) for all CoEnergy Trading Company deals as of Dec 31, 2000.  If you can export into excel and forward by e-mail, that would be appreciated."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/214.eml (Cross Timbers, forwarded to Ryder): "Sorry for the late notice on this one.  Can you provide MTM values as of Dec 29, 2000, for the short name of CROSS TIMBERS."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/137.eml (Gossett to 5 desk heads, forwarded by Giron to Carole Frank, 3/21/2001): "Two more counterparties need MTM values for Dec. 29, 2000." / "Please provide the total MTM value for that date within your region."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Finish and prioritise the back-dated counterparty valuation view that Confirmations already describes, or as an interim step give Confirmations a read-only standing query: MTM by counterparty short name and as-of date across all regions, with Delta/Vol columns left out. Confirmations runs it and sends it to the auditor without involving Risk.

AFTERWARDS
One person in Confirmations runs one report per request. There's no fan-out to 5–6 desk heads, no forwarding to analysts, no manual redaction, and no consolidation of regional replies.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: "we recieve several per week" (241). I take 3 a week ≈ 13 a month.
- Minutes today per request (all people): 5 desk heads × ~2 min to read and forward (10) + 5 regional analysts × ~10 min average to run, export and redact a mini-book, since some regions will have few or no deals (50) + Confirmations consolidating and replying ~10 = about 70 min.
- Afterwards: Confirmations runs the report and sends it in about 15 min. That time stays with Confirmations and is counted against the saving. Saved about 55 min per request.
- 13 × 55 = 715 min ≈ 11.9 hours/month × $85 ≈ $1,013/month (≈ $12,200/yr). One-time build cost is not included.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Group,

I received a call from Warren McReynold at the BPA today.  Warren was concerned with the level of service that our group is providing.  Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour.  The group at BPA cannot close their accounting books and meet reliability performance measures without our information.  I am meeting with Warren on Tuesday.  Warren is inclined to recommend to BPA that we are incapable of this service because of our inconsistent performance.  Such a recommendation would severely limit Enron's ability to produce value for our service customers in the near term and would likely prevent us from attracting new customers.  I believe that we can provide Warren's group with the information that it needs with minimal impact to our trading.

Therefore: 

We must call Grays Harbor and Frontier at the top of EVERY hour.  Then we need to call BPA and communicate the ACTUAL energy generated, not an estimate.  Finally, sign off the hour in the services book.  Les has provided us with the needed information for each day. Reserves can only be used for the hour that we are in, than we must resupply the schedule from a different source by working with the BPA marketers. If you have a question regarding reserves or pulling a schedule--please call Les or me.

If this process takes more than 5 minutes, please let me know. It is each trader's responsibilty to make this work.  It should be noted that we need to do this even if the generator is prescheduled, and must to continue to do this until these generators are automatically metered.  And yes, we will be compensated by the Services desk for our work. 

This service is a priority and should be treated as such.

Please see me with your comments and concerns regarding this job function.

Thanks,
Bill

Group,

I received a call from Warren McReynold at the BPA today.  Warren was concerned with the level of service that our group is providing.  Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour. I believe that we can provide Warren's group with the information that it needs with minimal impact to our trading.

Therefore: 

We must call Grays Harbor and Frontier at the top of EVERY hour.  Then we need to call BPA and communicate the ACTUAL energy generated, not an estimate.  Finally, sign off the hour in the services book.  Les has provided us with the needed information for each day. 3	1. Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls. ($3,102.50 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/335.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml
4	
5	# Rejected
6	
7	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
8	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
9	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
10	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
12	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
14	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
15	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
16

{
  "name": "Requests to extend expired deals at flowing meters",
  "today": "Gas keeps flowing at a meter after its Sitara deal ends, or on days the deal does not cover. The allocator (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Mary Poorman and others) finds it on the allocation exception screen or a feedback-error list after the month, parks the gas on Strangers Gas, and emails Daren Farmer about that one meter. Daren checks with the trader or contract admin and extends the deal or enters a new one; only then can accounting build an accounting arrangement and the allocator reallocate. Many volumes are tiny, the same meters come back month after month, and threads stall when the person who owns the deal is out or on another desk.",
  "change": "Warn the desk before month-end about deals ending at meters that still flow, and roll steady meters and tiny overflow volumes forward by rule instead of by email.",
  "explanation": "A list run before month-end matches meters with recent flow against Sitara deals that end that month, so Daren or the trader can extend or end each deal before the allocator finds the gap. Deals at meters that flow every month are entered as evergreen when the contract allows it, with the evergreen flag checked against the contract term at entry. Volumes under a small tolerance on days just past a deal's end attach to the prior deal by a rule the desk agrees in advance. Allocators then email Daren only about real renegotiations or contract questions, such as the Duke deal at meter 5892.",

27	What is MTM value?

29	What do you consider stress in the workplace?  How do you handle stress?  
30	Examples of a stressful situation?

43	
44	To: Jeffrey C Gossett/HOU/ECT@ECT
45	cc: David Baumbach/HOU/ECT@ECT, Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT, Kam 
46	Keiser/HOU/ECT@ECT, Errol McLaughlin/Corp/Enron@ENRON 
47	Subject: Technical Questions
48	
49	I also do not have many tech questions.  I look for trainability as well.  
50	
51	My questions:
52	-What do you know about the commodities market?
53	-Do you do any online trading, if so what, and why - looking for trading of 
54	options,  stocks, futs, etc for more difficult follow-up questions like
55	    why options, not buy/sell the underlying.  How do you determine what to 
56	trade and when, how long do you hold it.  Also looking for how often they 
57	play        on the internet and whether they do it at work.  
58	-What do you know about the industry?  How many units in a contract?  How do 
59	you hedge physical gas?  Financial positions?  
60	-What is V@R?  Not looking for a technical answer, just if they are familiar 
61	with the concept?  What other trading controls do they expect to be in place?
62	-How well do you handle ridicule?  (Always looking for a certain central 
63	trader's new lackey)
64	-How well versed are you in Excel?  What have you done where you are using 
65	excel to improve your work product?  How did you learn it?  Have you shared 
66	it with anyone else?  What other improvements have you made?  Would you give 
67	me a name of a person I could verify the impact this has had in your current 
68	organization?  (I don't ever call, I just am looking to see if there answer 
69	is the truth and what kind of ego they have) 
70	-Further educational goals?  MBA, CFA,  - looking for goals and motivators.
71	-Are you easily incited to violence?
72	
73	WK
74	
75	
76	---------------------- Forwarded by William Kelly/HOU/ECT on 12/27/2000 10:42

86	Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT, Errol McLaughlin/Corp/Enron@ENRON 
87	Subject: Technical Questions
88	
89	I do not have very many technical questions but here a the few that I have 
90	used:
91	
92	- Do you understand what curveshift is?  If so ... Price today was $10.20 and 
93	yesterday it was $10.13 ... what was my curveshift?
94	- What makes up a P&L statement?
95	- What is MTM accounting?  accrual accounting?
96	- If they have knowledge of options, what is a delta position?
97	
98	I guess these are more general analytical questions:
99	
100	- Give me an example of an problem you've had and how you solved it?
101	- The "eight ball" question (basic problem solving)
102	- The "light switch" question (advanced problem solving)
103	
104	When I interview I am looking for trainability, better than average problem 
105	solving skills and a desire to work in this environment.  If the candidate 
106	has these skills then I believe we can teach them what they need to know.  I 
107	also think it is candidates with these basic attributes that are a better fit 
108	for us.  They know they don't know everything (about Risk) and work hard to 
109	get up to speed. 
110	
111	Dave

RECORDED in decisions.md.

1	# Saved
2	
3	1. Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls. ($3,102.50 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/335.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml
4	
5	# Rejected
6	
7	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
8	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
9	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
10	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
12	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
14	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
15	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
16	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
17	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
18

content.text:
I rejected the proposal and recorded the rejection. Two other critics had already rejected this same work, for the same reasons listed in `decisions.md`.

**What is accurate:** Ricky Archer at Calpine does email a Word attachment called "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc" to the HPL scheduler. There are about 23 copies in Daren Farmer's Logistics folder, running from February 2000 to April 2001. The recipient did change from Lloyd to Juliann Kemp, and there are revised resends (773) and combined daily-and-monthly nominations (1245, 1370). The quotes you cited are real.

**What the mail does not support (these are problems with the evidence):**
- **A phone call every day.** Only 4 of about 23 nominations mention a call (1027, 1099, 880, 908). The message of 19 April 2001 (169.eml) says "will call if there are any changes", so calls look like they happen only when something changes. Your largest step, the 5-minute call, is mostly not there to save.
- **The "same as prior day" rule.** Nothing shows the volumes repeating from day to day. The mail shows the opposite: there are revised resends, monthly totals that move (79, 81 and 85 in 1063.eml), and force-majeure claims (1050, 681). The only support for unchanged volumes is giron-d/sent/795.eml. You were right not to rely on it: it has no date, its Message-ID is odd, and it is not a reply to Calpine.
- **HPL re-keying the Word document.** It is plausible, but no message shows it or how long it takes.
- **30 a month.** Weekend nominations arrive in one Friday message (1330.eml, "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination (weekend)"). So the work happens about once per working day, roughly 21 times a month.

Once the call and the no-change days are taken out, what is left is a guessed keying step of a few minutes on weekdays. The mail does not show that step.

**What could settle it:** look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for:
- what HPL does with each Calpine nomination: replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions;
- the contents of the nominations, to see how often volumes actually repeat;
- whether HPL had an electronic way for Calpine to enter nominations directly.

Evidence like that could support a smaller, weekday-only saving on the scheduler's keying step.

6	
7	# Rejected
8	
9	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
10	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
12	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
14	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
15	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
16	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
17	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
18	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
19	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
