Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.

content.text:
I saved the proposal, but only after fixing it. The idea holds up. The frequency and the minutes saved were too high, so the saved figure is much smaller than analyst-3's: **$45.90 a month instead of $340**.

**Quotes that were correct.** Every quote I checked appears in the mail as written: 1029, 1021, 1018, 899, 750, 1406, 2003 and 1458. The way the work is described also matches the mail: the allocator emails about one meter at a time, the gas waits on Strangers Gas, accounting waits for the deal extension, and threads stall when the deal owner is out.

**What was wrong:**
1. **"About 20 distinct requests in March–April 2000."** Several files listed as separate requests are copies of one thread:
   - 896, 897 and 899 are one thread.
   - 995 and 1000 are one thread.
   - 1055, 1059 and 1060 are one thread, and 898 is about the same meter (1520).

   That leaves about 13 separate requests over two months, and March–April was the busiest stretch.
2. **12 cases a month.** No message supports this rate. Requests go straight to Daren Farmer, so his folders should catch most of them, which makes "the archive is only part of the mail" a weak reason to scale up. Counted from February 2000 to March 2001, I found 31 separate requests, which the pipeline counts as **2.14 a month**.
3. **20 minutes saved on every case.** Many cases still need a trader's decision, and the rule can't remove that. Daren told the allocators to "run all wellhead deals through Tom Acton first" (899). The Duke deal "needs to be renegotiated" (1458). The contract in 1406 had no evergreen. I used **15 minutes**.
4. **"A new nightly report."** The allocators already find these gaps on the allocation exception screen and the feedback-error monitor. I reframed the report as a warning before month-end about deals ending at meters that still flow, so the desk can act before the allocator finds the gap.

**Why it isn't a duplicate.** In `decisions.md`, nothing similar was saved. Rejection 16 covers related work, but it was rejected on different evidence: Clem Cernosek's one-time burst of write-off memos, and rolling deals forward against the trader's word. That rejection asked for proof of a steady monthly flow of allocator requests and a change that respects renegotiation. This version gives both: 31 separate requests over 14 months, and evergreen only where the contract allows it, plus a small-volume rule the desk agrees in advance.

**Saved version:** 31 occurrences, no stated rate, 15 minutes each. That works out to 15 min × 2.14 a month = 0.54 hours = $45.90 a month. It is entry 2 in `decisions.md`.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because the same work has already been saved. The idea is sound and the mail supports it, but it can't be saved twice.

**Why it was rejected.** Another critic already saved "Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests" (item 2 in `decisions.md`, $1,381.25 a month). It cites the same four messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240 and 241). Its change is close to yours: a month-end file of each counterparty's official MTM by region, so Confirmations can answer auditors without asking the desks. The check also flagged that 3 of your 4 occurrences belong to that saved proposal. More research would not change this, so the rejection says none is needed. If you think a live, any-date query is clearly worth more than a month-end file, argue for amending the saved proposal rather than adding a second one.

**What I found while checking:**
- **Quotes:** all accurate. Message 136 is a useful extra occurrence. In it Carole Frank sends the West totals to Giron, who forwards them to Gossett, so the answer passes back through each desk head.
- **"Often late":** the mail doesn't support this. There is only one "Sorry for the late notice," from Hunter about the Cross Timbers request.
- **Who blacks out Delta/Vol:** the mail doesn't say whether the desk staff or Confirmations do it.
- **Who adds up the totals:** in 137 the regional totals go to Gossett, not Confirmations.
- **Your rate of 3 a week is probably high.** Every request in the mail asks for a Dec 29 or Dec 31, 2000 value and was sent in February or March. The work likely peaks in audit season, so "several per week" may not hold all year. My draft used 2 a week and 50 minutes, which came to about $614 a month.

I rejected this proposal because the same work has already been saved. The idea is sound and the mail supports it, but it can't be saved twice.

**Why it was rejected.** Another critic already saved "Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests" (item 2 in `decisions.md`, $1,381.25 a month). It cites the same four messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240 and 241). Its change is close to yours: a month-end file of each counterparty's official MTM by region, so Confirmations can answer auditors without asking the desks. The check also flagged that 3 of your 4 occurrences belong to that saved proposal. More research would not change this, so the rejection says none is needed. If you think a live, any-date query is clearly worth more than a month-end file, argue for amending the saved proposal rather than adding a second one.

**What I found while checking:**
- **Quotes:** all accurate. Message 136 is a useful extra occurrence. In it Carole Frank sends the West totals to Giron, who forwards them to Gossett, so the answer passes back through each desk head.
- **"Often late":** the mail doesn't support this. There is only one "Sorry for the late notice," from Hunter about the Cross Timbers request.
- **Who blacks out Delta/Vol:** the mail doesn't say whether the desk staff or Confirmations do it.
- **Who adds up the totals:** in 137 the regional totals go to Gossett, not Confirmations.
- **Your rate of 3 a week is probably high.** Every request in the mail asks for a Dec 29 or Dec 31, 2000 value and was sent in February or March. The work likely peaks in audit season, so "several per week" may not hold all year. My draft used 2 a week and 50 minutes, which came to about $614 a month.

TITLE: Put the West desk's rebook handler (or a desk mailbox) straight onto Credit's daily "Credit Report" distribution, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it by hand every business day

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Credit (Veronica Espinoza, Russell Diamond) emails a daily "Credit Report--<date>" to about 30–35 people. It lists TAGG deals to rebook to the correct counterparty entity, or pending with a named credit officer. The list includes desk heads such as Giron, but not the staff on his desk who actually do the rebooks. Giron then forwards each day's report by hand to Carole Frank (sometimes to others). When he's away, the reports pile up and get forwarded in a batch afterwards, so rebooks are delayed.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/182.eml: Subject "Credit Report--2/28/01". Giron forwards Veronica Espinoza's 2/28 09:18 AM report to Carole Frank at 09:20 AM; the original To: list has ~35 names, including "Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT" but not Carole Frank.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/154.eml: Subject "Credit Report 3/12/01", forwarded 3/19/2001: "I don't know if you got any of these while I was out." The forwarded report has lines such as "Dynegy Energy Inc.    qW2360.1 Rebook to Dynegy Marketing & Trade" and "Engage Energy Canada LP   qW3304.1 Rebook from ENA to ECC (Under the ISDA)".
- corpus/giron-d/sent/10.eml and 11.eml (both sent 9 May 2001 06:37): Subjects "Credit Report--5/9/01" and "Credit Report--5/8/01". Two days forwarded together to Carole Frank, so the 5/8 report reached her the next day.
- Volume: giron-d/sent has 71 such forwards (Subject "Credit Report…", From darron.giron, to Carole Frank or a desk member) dated from 2 Feb 2001 (267.eml, 264.eml) to 9 May 2001 (10.eml). That's about 3.2 months, or about 22 a month, which matches one per business day.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Credit adds Carole Frank (and any backup) or a West-desk group mailbox to the Credit Report distribution list. This is a one-time list change. Optionally, Credit tags each line with the book or desk so each desk's handler sees only their lines.

AFTERWARDS
The rebook handler gets the report at the same time as the desk head. Giron does nothing. Reports no longer pile up when he's out of the office, and same-day rebooks aren't held up by a forward.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: daily on business days. The reports are dated per day ("Credit Report--2/28/01", "--5/8/01", "--5/9/01"), and there are 71 forwards in about 3.2 months ≈ 22 a month.
- Minutes saved per occurrence: about 2 min of Giron's time to open, forward and address each report (or batch). Carole's reading time is unchanged and not counted.
- 22 × 2 = 44 min ≈ 0.73 hours/month × $85 ≈ $62/month. This is a conservative figure for one desk. Other desk heads on the list probably relay the report the same way, but I haven't counted that because this archive doesn't show it.

9	# Rejected

11	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
12	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
14	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Not in decisions.md as of my last read.)

TITLE: Extend the existing EOL/TAGG auto-booking rule (already used for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada) to every counterparty ECC has a master agreement with, so Canadian deals book straight into FT-US/CAND-ERMS instead of being found and "flipped" by hand from Houston books before each month's NYMEX invoicing

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Deals with Canadian counterparties that must settle with ECC (Aquila Canada Corp., Duke Energy Marketing LP, Engage Energy Canada, Dynegy Canada) get booked, often automatically by EOL, into Houston books (FT-West, MGMT-WEST, FT-Ontario and others) as ENA deals. Each month around NYMEX close, Stacey Vallejo (Calgary) finds some of them and emails 6–7 Houston desk heads. Each desk head forwards the email to their book administrators, who search every book and move the deals by hand. Deals that are missed hold up invoicing, and liquidations have to be re-run.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/550.eml (Oct 2000): "There are a few deals in the MGMT-WEST book that need to be moved to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS BOOK.  These are all EnronOnline deals so they were put into this book automatically." / "Nymex closes today, and I'm going to have to start invoicing on Monday, so I need to have all deals with ECC in the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by the end of today."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/292.eml (Jan 2001, sent to 6 desk heads and forwarded by Giron to 5 staff: "Please flip these if applicable."): about 35 deal IDs across FT-CENT, FT-East, FT-Northwest, FT-NY, FT-Ontario, FT-West and GD-New. "Please go through your books to see if there are any deals that I might have missed." / "I've spoken to Jennifer Denny with EOL about getting a program set up for Duke deals similar to ones we have with TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada so they automatically get booked to settle with ECC, but I don't think this has happened yet."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/192.eml (Feb 2001, forwarded by Giron to 7 staff): "These deals are showing up in TAGG as settling with ENA, could you all please keep an eye out for deals with this company and flip them right away."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/168.eml (Mar 2001): "This is causing problems with the February Liquidations as I settled this deal with Aquila, but it isn't coming through the liquidations correctly.  Please let me know when this is done so I can let Shannon McPearson know that she needs to re-run the February Liquidations."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/108.eml (Mar 2001, to 7 people): "I have a feeling that there are lots of deals like this in TAGG, but I just don't know where." / "What I'm requesting is that you go through all your books and look for all deals with Aquila Canada Corp." / "As it stands, I'm missing at least 10 deals from the April 2001 Nymex invoice"
- Other occurrences, Oct 2000 to Mar 2001: giron-d/sent/551, 539, 535, 460, 459, 419, 407, 406, 405, 404, 360, 270, 250, 246, 195, 164, 127, 114, 110, 23.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
EOL and TAGG get a counterparty-to-entity booking rule for every counterparty on ECC's master list, the same mechanism Stacey says already exists for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada. Deals then book to FT-US/CAND-ERMS settling with ECC from the start. When ECC signs a new master (as with Aquila Canada in 192), the counterparty is added to the rule instead of a broadcast going out. A monthly TAGG query of "ECC-master counterparties in non-ECC books" replaces the manual book-by-book searches for any leftovers.

AFTERWARDS
No monthly broadcast, no forwarding chain through desk heads, no book-by-book search by about 10 book admins, and no re-run liquidations. Stacey checks one exception query before invoicing.

ESTIMATE (one cycle per month, the conservative choice; the mail shows several messages in most months)
- Frequency: monthly, tied to NYMEX close and invoicing ("Nymex closes today, and I'm going to have to start invoicing", 550; "Nymex settled yesterday for April, so invoicing for these deals is taking place today", 108). Occurrences appear every month from Oct 2000 to Mar 2001.
- Minutes per cycle today: Stacey identifies deals and writes the requests and follow-ups, ~30. Six desk heads read and forward, 6 × 3 = 18. About 10 book admins search their books and flip deals, 10 × 12 = 120. Total ≈ 168 min, not counting the occasional liquidation re-run (168).
- Afterwards: Stacey runs one exception query and a book admin flips any leftovers, ~25 min. Saved ≈ 143 min per month.
- 143 min ≈ 2.4 hours/month × $85 ≈ $203/month (≈ $2,430/yr).

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

TITLE: Extend the existing EOL/TAGG auto-booking rule (already used for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada) to every counterparty ECC has a master agreement with, so Canadian deals book straight into FT-US/CAND-ERMS instead of being found and "flipped" by hand from Houston books before each month's NYMEX invoicing

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Deals with Canadian counterparties that must settle with ECC (Aquila Canada Corp., Duke Energy Marketing LP, Engage Energy Canada, Dynegy Canada) get booked, often automatically by EOL, into Houston books (FT-West, MGMT-WEST, FT-Ontario and others) as ENA deals. Each month around NYMEX close, Stacey Vallejo (Calgary) finds some of them and emails 6–7 Houston desk heads. Each desk head forwards the email to their book administrators, who search every book and move the deals by hand. Deals that are missed hold up invoicing, and liquidations have to be re-run.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/550.eml (Oct 2000): "There are a few deals in the MGMT-WEST book that need to be moved to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS BOOK.  These are all EnronOnline deals so they were put into this book automatically." / "Nymex closes today, and I'm going to have to start invoicing on Monday, so I need to have all deals with ECC in the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by the end of today."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/292.eml (Jan 2001, sent to 6 desk heads and forwarded by Giron to 5 staff: "Please flip these if applicable."): about 35 deal IDs across FT-CENT, FT-East, FT-Northwest, FT-NY, FT-Ontario, FT-West and GD-New. "Please go through your books to see if there are any deals that I might have missed." / "I've spoken to Jennifer Denny with EOL about getting a program set up for Duke deals similar to ones we have with TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada so they automatically get booked to settle with ECC, but I don't think this has happened yet."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/192.eml (Feb 2001, forwarded by Giron to 7 staff): "These deals are showing up in TAGG as settling with ENA, could you all please keep an eye out for deals with this company and flip them right away."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/168.eml (Mar 2001): "This is causing problems with the February Liquidations as I settled this deal with Aquila, but it isn't coming through the liquidations correctly.  Please let me know when this is done so I can let Shannon McPearson know that she needs to re-run the February Liquidations."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/108.eml (Mar 2001, to 7 people): "I have a feeling that there are lots of deals like this in TAGG, but I just don't know where." / "What I'm requesting is that you go through all your books and look for all deals with Aquila Canada Corp." / "As it stands, I'm missing at least 10 deals from the April 2001 Nymex invoice"
- Other occurrences, Oct 2000 to Mar 2001: giron-d/sent/551, 539, 535, 460, 459, 419, 407, 406, 405, 404, 360, 270, 250, 246, 195, 164, 127, 114, 110, 23.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
EOL and TAGG get a counterparty-to-entity booking rule for every counterparty on ECC's master list, the same mechanism Stacey says already exists for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada. Deals then book to FT-US/CAND-ERMS settling with ECC from the start. When ECC signs a new master (as with Aquila Canada in 192), the counterparty is added to the rule instead of a broadcast going out. A monthly TAGG query of "ECC-master counterparties in non-ECC books" replaces the manual book-by-book searches for any leftovers.

AFTERWARDS
No monthly broadcast, no forwarding chain through desk heads, no book-by-book search by about 10 book admins, and no re-run liquidations. Stacey checks one exception query before invoicing.

ESTIMATE (one cycle per month, the conservative choice; the mail shows several messages in most months)
- Frequency: monthly, tied to NYMEX close and invoicing ("Nymex closes today, and I'm going to have to start invoicing", 550; "Nymex settled yesterday for April, so invoicing for these deals is taking place today", 108). Occurrences appear every month from Oct 2000 to Mar 2001.
- Minutes per cycle today: Stacey identifies deals and writes the requests and follow-ups, ~30. Six desk heads read and forward, 6 × 3 = 18. About 10 book admins search their books and flip deals, 10 × 12 = 120. Total ≈ 168 min, not counting the occasional liquidation re-run (168).
- Afterwards: Stacey runs one exception query and a book admin flips any leftovers, ~25 min. Saved ≈ 143 min per month.
- 143 min ≈ 2.4 hours/month × $85 ≈ $203/month (≈ $2,430/yr).

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.

1	{
2	  "name": "Requests to extend expired deals at flowing meters",
3	  "today": "Gas keeps flowing at a meter after its Sitara deal ends, or on days the deal does not cover. The allocator (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Mary Poorman and others) finds it on the allocation exception screen or a feedback-error list after the month, parks the gas on Strangers Gas, and emails Daren Farmer about that one meter. Daren checks with the trader or contract admin and extends the deal or enters a new one; only then can accounting build an accounting arrangement and the allocator reallocate. Many volumes are tiny, the same meters come back month after month, and threads stall when the person who owns the deal is out or on another desk.",
4	  "change": "Warn the desk before month-end about deals ending at meters that still flow, and roll steady meters and tiny overflow volumes forward by rule instead of by email.",

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Not in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md lines 273, 303, 310 mention it.)

TITLE: Replace the pay-period "Time Reports Due" email round on the Transwestern commercial team with self-service absence entry and an automatic reminder (standard hours by default), so the assistant no longer collects absences by email

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Every pay period, the team assistant (Audrey Robertson, Transwestern Pipeline) emails the 7-person team to send her their time reports. Each person replies by email with their vacation, sick and holiday days. She reads and records them, sometimes queries or corrects them, and sends reminders when replies don't come in. The round happens even when nobody has anything unusual to report.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/13.eml (13 Dec 2001): Robertson to 7 people (Donoho, Lindberg, Lohman, Lokay, McConnell, Watson, Y'barbo): "Time Reports Are Due!!!" / "Please submit...." Lokay: "I took 1/2 day vacation Friday, December 7.  Thanks." Robertson: "What about tomorrow?" Lokay: "I don't know if I am taking 1/2 day of vacation yet..." Robertson: "Let's just see what tomorrow brings (smile)." That's five messages to settle one person's time.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/56.eml (3 Jan 2002): "Send me your time reports today." Reply: "I took my last day of vacation on Wednesday, Dec 26."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml (31 Jan 2002): "Time Reports Due Today!!!" / "Please submit!!!" Reply: "I was out Friday, the 25th, and would like to use my \"discretionary holiday\"!"
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/99.eml (13–14 Feb 2002): "Don't forget to submit your time reports by Thursday morning." Lokay: "I was out sick yesterday afternoon, 02/13, and will be taking vacation tomorrow, 02/15." Robertson corrects: "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay...."
- Also 11.eml, 12.eml (13 Dec 2001), 92.eml (14 Feb 2002), 115.eml (28 Feb 2002 "Time Reports are Due!!"), 142.eml (14 Mar 2002 "Time Reports Due Tomorrow").
- Cadence from the dates: 13 Dec, 3 Jan, 31 Jan, 14 Feb, 28 Feb, 14 Mar. That's every two weeks, so a biweekly pay period, about 2.17 rounds a month.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Employees record their own absences in the company time system (self-service) as they happen. Anyone who records nothing is paid standard hours by default. The system sends the deadline reminder automatically and lists only missing or odd entries for the assistant to approve.

AFTERWARDS
No broadcast reminder, no email replies to read and transcribe, and no back-and-forth to clarify. The assistant approves a short exception list.

ESTIMATE (assistant's time only; the employees' reply emails are about the same effort as typing an entry, so I count nothing saved for them)
- Frequency: every pay period, about every 2 weeks (dates above), ≈ 2.17 a month.
- Assistant's minutes per round today: write the reminder and any follow-up ~3, read and record ~7 replies ~2 min each = 14, clarify or correct (13.eml, 99.eml) ~3. Total ≈ 20 min.
- Afterwards: approve exceptions ~5 min. Saved ≈ 15 min per round.
- 15 × 2.17 ≈ 33 min ≈ 0.54 hours/month × $85 ≈ $46/month for this one team. It's small, but the same pattern probably repeats on other teams that have an assistant. I haven't counted those because the archive doesn't show them.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Not in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md lines 273, 303, 310 mention it.)

TITLE: Replace the pay-period "Time Reports Due" email round on the Transwestern commercial team with self-service absence entry and an automatic reminder (standard hours by default), so the assistant no longer collects absences by email

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Every pay period, the team assistant (Audrey Robertson, Transwestern Pipeline) emails the 7-person team to send her their time reports. Each person replies by email with their vacation, sick and holiday days. She reads and records them, sometimes queries or corrects them, and sends reminders when replies don't come in. The round happens even when nobody has anything unusual to report.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/13.eml (13 Dec 2001): Robertson to 7 people (Donoho, Lindberg, Lohman, Lokay, McConnell, Watson, Y'barbo): "Time Reports Are Due!!!" / "Please submit...." Lokay: "I took 1/2 day vacation Friday, December 7.  Thanks." Robertson: "What about tomorrow?" Lokay: "I don't know if I am taking 1/2 day of vacation yet..." Robertson: "Let's just see what tomorrow brings (smile)." That's five messages to settle one person's time.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/56.eml (3 Jan 2002): "Send me your time reports today." Reply: "I took my last day of vacation on Wednesday, Dec 26."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml (31 Jan 2002): "Time Reports Due Today!!!" / "Please submit!!!" Reply: "I was out Friday, the 25th, and would like to use my \"discretionary holiday\"!"
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/99.eml (13–14 Feb 2002): "Don't forget to submit your time reports by Thursday morning." Lokay: "I was out sick yesterday afternoon, 02/13, and will be taking vacation tomorrow, 02/15." Robertson corrects: "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay...."
- Also 11.eml, 12.eml (13 Dec 2001), 92.eml (14 Feb 2002), 115.eml (28 Feb 2002 "Time Reports are Due!!"), 142.eml (14 Mar 2002 "Time Reports Due Tomorrow").
- Cadence from the dates: 13 Dec, 3 Jan, 31 Jan, 14 Feb, 28 Feb, 14 Mar. That's every two weeks, so a biweekly pay period, about 2.17 rounds a month.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Employees record their own absences in the company time system (self-service) as they happen. Anyone who records nothing is paid standard hours by default. The system sends the deadline reminder automatically and lists only missing or odd entries for the assistant to approve.

AFTERWARDS
No broadcast reminder, no email replies to read and transcribe, and no back-and-forth to clarify. The assistant approves a short exception list.

ESTIMATE (assistant's time only; the employees' reply emails are about the same effort as typing an entry, so I count nothing saved for them)
- Frequency: every pay period, about every 2 weeks (dates above), ≈ 2.17 a month.
- Assistant's minutes per round today: write the reminder and any follow-up ~3, read and record ~7 replies ~2 min each = 14, clarify or correct (13.eml, 99.eml) ~3. Total ≈ 20 min.
- Afterwards: approve exceptions ~5 min. Saved ≈ 15 min per round.
- 15 × 2.17 ≈ 33 min ≈ 0.54 hours/month × $85 ≈ $46/month for this one team. It's small, but the same pattern probably repeats on other teams that have an assistant. I haven't counted those because the archive doesn't show them.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

24	Subject:	Columbia Gulf order on negotiated rates
25	
26	I received a copy of an order issued by the FERc on Columbia negotiated rate transaction, which includes a formula ie indexed rate.  They accepted the negotiated rate deal but they are requiring  them to file in their tariff within ONE DAY after the rate has been determined the contract and actual rate. ( Each time the actual rate changes during the term)   Just think about this for the upcoming TW_ USGT deal and NNG"- Reliant deals.    Notwithstanding the time to actually make the filing, the cost to serve it each day if the negotiated rate is different by day and then the service when an order is issued each day---  I believe this is FERC's way to attempt to eliminate negotiated rate indexed based deals-  they are punishing themselves as well, as each filing will require a notice etc-  so every day they could need to issue an order.   
27	
28	I feel we need to discuss with Columbia, INGAA and join in filing for rehearing on this administrative nightmare.  An alternative would be to require you to post on Internet website the day of the transaction the actual rate, so similarly situated customers would have access to the actual rate.  I'm sending you guys a copy of the order.

Subject:	Columbia Gulf order on negotiated rates

I received a copy of an order issued by the FERc on Columbia negotiated rate transaction, which includes a formula ie indexed rate.  They accepted the negotiated rate deal but they are requiring  them to file in their tariff within ONE DAY after the rate has been determined the contract and actual rate. ( Each time the actual rate changes during the term)   Just think about this for the upcoming TW_ USGT deal and NNG"- Reliant deals.    Notwithstanding the time to actually make the filing, the cost to serve it each day if the negotiated rate is different by day and then the service when an order is issued each day---  I believe this is FERC's way to attempt to eliminate negotiated rate indexed based deals-  they are punishing themselves as well, as each filing will require a notice etc-  so every day they could need to issue an order.   

I feel we need to discuss with Columbia, INGAA and join in filing for rehearing on this administrative nightmare.  An alternative would be to require you to post on Internet website the day of the transaction the actual rate, so similarly situated customers would have access to the actual rate.  I'm sending you guys a copy of the order.

  "name": "Flipping Canadian (ECC) deals out of Houston books before NYMEX invoicing",
  "today": "Deals with counterparties that must settle with Enron Canada (ECC), such as Aquila Canada Corp., Duke Energy Marketing, Engage Energy Canada and Dynegy Canada, get booked into Houston books (MGMT-WEST, FT-West, FT-Ontario, G-DAILY-EST and others) as ENA deals, often automatically by EnronOnline. Around each NYMEX close, Stacey Vallejo in Calgary finds some of them and emails six to eight Houston desk heads. Each desk head, such as Darron Giron, forwards the email to five to seven book administrators, who search their books and move the deals by hand to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book. Stacey cannot invoice until this is done; deals that are missed leave gaps in the NYMEX invoice and can force liquidations to be re-run. An automatic booking rule already exists for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada, but not for the other counterparties.",
  "change": "Extend the existing EnronOnline/TAGG rule that books deals straight to ECC to every counterparty ECC has a master agreement with, and replace the monthly book-by-book search with one exception query.",

When ECC signs a new master agreement, as with Aquila Canada in February 2001, the counterparty is added to the rule instead of a broadcast going out. Because the existing rule has not caught every deal (a Dynegy Canada deal still needed flipping in February 2001) and deals booked by hand bypass it, a standing TAGG report of ECC-master counterparties in non-ECC books, like the search Stacey showed Sherry Dawson, is run before each NYMEX close. Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Not in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md line 142 mentions it.)

TITLE: Set up the GLO/EGM gas/crude swap once as term deals with formula pricing (a zero-price HPL→GLO sale for the whole term, and HPL→ENA / ENA→EGM demand tickets priced by formula from the gas index × firm volume and from the prior month's crude value) instead of rebuilding and repricing tickets by hand every month before flash

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Under the GLO/EGM gas-for-crude arrangement, Settlements and Risk agreed a 4-ticket accounting treatment. Bryce Baxter spelled out three steps that must be done by hand every month before flash. When the monthly ticket was copied from an earlier month, the price wasn't zeroed, and four or more people then spent weeks finding and fixing it.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/175.eml (Bryce Baxter, 3/5/2001): "This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward:" / "The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly." / "The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out." / "The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM." / "This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value."
- Same file, the rework (Joanie Ngo, 4/16/2001, forwarded by Julie Meyers to Daren Farmer 4/17 with "What do you think?"): "Deal 640685 for March 01 production:  per Daren Farmer (in the Audit field in Sitara), this was copied from deal #547201.  This deal is the Crude Swap where volume stayed but price got zeroed out and booked as a demand charge under 679847 and 679848." / "Please confirm that it is the Crude Swap and rebook as necessary." Julie Meyers had earlier (3/19) zeroed 547201 and 591307 and created 679847, 679848 and 679859 by hand for Jan and Feb.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/30.eml (Megan Parker, 10/31/2001) shows the monthly GLO deal series still needing manual tracing later: "Jan 01		547201 / Feb 01		591307 / Mar 01		640685 / Apr 01		692167 / May 01		755787" and "I can follow the ENA deals in path Manager, but I am having a hard time with the HPLC deals."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Book the HPL→GLO sale once for the term at zero price, so there's no monthly zeroing and no copy errors. Book the HPL→ENA and ENA-Wellhead purchase demand tickets once, with a formula demand amount (firm volume × the month's gas index) that Sitara/Unify calculates when the index posts. Book the ENA→EGM demand ticket once, with the amount taken from the crude value EGM already reports for the prior month, entered as a single number in one place each month.

AFTERWARDS
Each month, the only manual input is the prior month's crude value, entered once. The gas-side demand charges calculate themselves from the index. There are no monthly zero-outs, and no copied tickets that come back with the wrong price for Settlements and Risk to chase.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly ("This will require the following steps be taken monthly", "This needs to be done monthly prior to flash", 175.eml). The deal ran at least Jan–May 2001 (30.eml).
- Minutes today per month: zero the HPL→GLO price ~5; calculate the gas value (index × volume) and update two demand tickets ~15; update the EGM crude demand ticket ~5; Settlements and Risk checking the monthly entries before flash ~10. About 35 min of routine work. On top of that is rework when a copy goes wrong: in March 2001 it involved Ngo, Herrera, Meyers and Farmer (about 60 min combined). Averaged at one occurrence per 5 months, that's about 12 min a month.
- Afterwards: enter the crude value once and glance at the result, ~8 min.
- Saved ≈ 35 + 12 − 8 = 39 min/month ≈ 0.65 hours × $85 ≈ $55/month (≈ $660/yr).

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

- Minutes today per month: zero the HPL→GLO price ~5; calculate the gas value (index × volume) and update two demand tickets ~15; update the EGM crude demand ticket ~5; Settlements and Risk checking the monthly entries before flash ~10. About 35 min of routine work. On top of that is rework when a copy goes wrong: in March 2001 it involved Ngo, Herrera, Meyers and Farmer (about 60 min combined). Averaged at one occurrence per 5 months, that's about 12 min a month.
- Afterwards: enter the crude value once and glance at the result, ~8 min.
- Saved ≈ 35 + 12 − 8 = 39 min/month ≈ 0.65 hours × $85 ≈ $55/month (≈ $660/yr).

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

85	Change the existing deals, 547201 and 591307, to a zero price.  This will eliminate the A/R balance on HPL's books for GLO, but will keep the volume nom'd to GLO and will not impact UA4.
86	Enter a ticket on HPL for a sale to ENA for the value of the gas that was zeroed out on the above tickets.  This should be entered as a demand charge only and the amounts should be $974,144 for 1/01 and $766,304 for 2/01.
87	Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book purchases the demand from HPL.  The amounts would be the same as in #2 above.
88	Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book sells demand to EGM for the value of the crude oil for the prior month.  For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60 (the 12/00 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).  For 2/01, the sale would be for $839,008.29 (the 1/01 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).

91	The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly.
92	The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out.
93	The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM.
94

This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value.   "name": "Flipping Canadian (ECC) deals out of Houston books before NYMEX invoicing",
  "today": "Deals with counterparties that must settle with Enron Canada (ECC), such as Aquila Canada Corp., Duke Energy Marketing, Engage Energy Canada and Dynegy Canada, get booked into Houston books (MGMT-WEST, FT-West, FT-Ontario, G-DAILY-EST and others) as ENA deals, often automatically by EnronOnline. Around each monthly NYMEX close, Stacey Vallejo in Calgary finds some of them and emails six to eight Houston desk heads. Desk heads forward the email to their book administrators (Darron Giron sends it on to five to seven people), who search their books and move the deals by hand to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book; single late finds follow in separate emails. Stacey cannot invoice until this is done; missed deals leave gaps in the NYMEX invoice and can force liquidations to be re-run. An automatic booking rule already exists for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada, but not for the other counterparties.",
  "change": "Extend the existing EnronOnline/TAGG rule that books deals straight to ECC to every counterparty ECC has a master agreement with, and replace the monthly book-by-book search with one exception query.",
  "explanation": "The EnronOnline team (Jennifer Denny was already asked about Duke) adds every counterparty on ECC's master-agreement list to the rule that books TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada deals to settle with ECC, so those deals land in FT-US/CAND-ERMS from the start. When ECC signs a new master agreement, as with Aquila Canada in February 2001, the counterparty is added to the rule instead of a broadcast going out. Because the existing rule has not caught every deal (a Dynegy Canada deal still needed flipping in February 2001) and deals booked by hand bypass it, a standing TAGG report of ECC-master counterparties in non-ECC books, like the search Stacey showed Sherry Dawson, is run before each NYMEX close. content.text: I'm looking into how Producer Services wellhead tickets get re-keyed, to see if there's enough frequency evidence. Three proposals are still with the critic.

I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. Someone has already saved the same work: decisions.md Saved item 3, "Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals" ($364.65 a month). It proposes essentially the same change: book every ECC counterparty's deals straight to FT-US/CAND-ERMS, and use a list of exceptions instead of a search of every book. It also cites the same Giron messages: 108, 195, 292 and 550. Three earlier versions of this idea were already rejected as duplicates of that item (decisions.md lines 33, 40 and one more). The problem is not the idea or the evidence, so more research would not change the verdict.

The evidence itself held up. I read 550, 292, 192, 168, 108, 460, 404, 270, 250, 195, 110 and 23, and the quotes and the described process are accurate. Three things would have needed fixing if it weren't a duplicate:

- **Occurrences counted several times per month.** Many of the 22 files are follow-ups within the same monthly cycle (for example 192 and 195 on Feb 26, 168 on Mar 5, and 108 and 110 on Mar 28–29). Counted as separate times, they inflate the rate to about 1.4 a month. With one occurrence per cycle it is about 0.75 a month (7 cycles from Oct 2000 to May 2001).
- **The existing rule leaks.** A Dynegy Canada deal still had to be flipped in Feb 2001 (250), even though Dynegy Canada already has the automatic booking rule. Extending the rule alone would not end the hand flips; the leftover-deal query is required, not optional.
- **The number of book admins is a guess.** Only Giron's own forwards are visible (5 to 7 people). The figure of "about 10 book admins" across all desks is not in the mail.

content.text:
I didn't save this proposal and recorded it as rejected. Another critic had already saved the same work, "Twice-monthly time report email round at Transwestern". When I checked `decisions.md` just before saving, it had no entry about time reports. But `save` then refused, because 5 of my 6 occurrences already belong to that saved proposal. The other critic must have saved it in between. Your idea and evidence held up; it's only a duplicate. More research wouldn't change that.

**What I checked, in case it helps with the saved version:**
- All the quotes you cited are accurate.
- Three claims went further than the mail shows, so I left them out of my draft:
  - **Chasing late replies:** nothing shows her chasing people who hadn't replied. The 13 Feb email in 92.eml and 99.eml is a reminder sent the day before the Thursday deadline, not a follow-up.
  - **"Robertson corrects":** her line in 99.eml, "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay....", is unclear. It reads better as a query than a correction.
  - **Recording the replies:** the mail shows replies coming to her. It doesn't show her entering them, though that's a fair guess.
- **The change is realistic.** Enron staff already had accounts on its self-service HR site, eHRonline (SAP). corpus/williams-w3/inbox/61.eml shows this, which supports self-service entry without buying anything.
- **How often:** 11, 12 and 13.eml are the same 13 Dec round, and 92 and 99.eml are the same 14 Feb round. So there are 6 separate rounds, not 9 messages' worth. The 2002 dates are two weeks apart. The pipeline's count from those six dates came to only 1.25 a month, so it understates the real rate of about 2 a month.
- **Minutes:** I would have used 12 minutes saved per round rather than 15. Each of the seven replies takes about a minute to read and type in, plus the reminder and the occasional query. The pipeline's check came to about $21 a month.

26:- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
34:- Flipping ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books: Have EOL/TAGG book deals with ECC's master-swap counterparties straight to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, with a daily exception report, instead of manual search-and-flip requests.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals', which cites the same Giron messages.
38:- Monthly flip of ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books before NYMEX invoicing: Extend the EOL auto-booking program to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties and run a nightly TAGG exception query for misbooked ENA deals, replacing the monthly all-books sweep.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' ($364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages (108, 114, 195, 292, 360, 407) and already books every ECC counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically with a daily list of deals that slip through.
41:- Monthly sweep to flip ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Book deals with ECC master-swap counterparties to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically at capture, and replace the all-desk monthly sweep with one exception query.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' (decisions.md Saved item 3, $364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages 108, 195, 292 and 360.
- Monthly sweep to flip ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Book deals with ECC master-swap counterparties to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically at capture, and replace the all-desk monthly sweep with one exception query.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' (decisions.md Saved item 3, $364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages 108, 195, 292 and 360.
- Flipping Canadian (ECC) deals out of Houston books before NYMEX invoicing: Extend the existing EnronOnline/TAGG rule that books deals straight to ECC to every counterparty ECC has a master agreement with, and replace the monthly book-by-book search with one exception query.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' (decisions.md Saved item 3, $364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages 108, 195, 292 and 550.
- Nightly schedule checkout calls with counterparties, Portland Real Time desk: Match prescheduled paths against e-tags automatically each night so traders phone only counterparties with a mismatch or cut.. Why: The only evidence is one memo launching the Enpower Path Confirmation tool two weeks before Enron's bankruptcy and the desk's move to UBS. The 2-minute call time is made up. The BPA precedent is a different party doing the calls, not matching. And a later message shows the tag data the matching would depend on leaves Enron's schedules out, which is the kind of error the calls catch. Research that could settle it: Look for messages after December 2001 (UBS Warburg Energy period) showing the nightly checkout still running with many counterparties, how long it takes, and whether tag data is complete enough to confirm schedules without a call.
- Collecting pay-period time reports by email on the Transwestern commercial team: Have staff record their own absences in eHRonline/SAP with standard hours as the default, so the assistant only reviews exceptions instead of collecting replies by email.. Why: The same work is already saved as "Twice-monthly time report email round at Transwestern", which uses 5 of the same 6 occurrences.
- Correcting mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams: Have the directory admins give both Bill Williams address-book entries distinguishing display names (office and group) so senders stop picking the wrong one.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md (item 8, 'Correcting mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams', citing 110, 184, 255, 259, 437, 448, 450, 471, 492, 493, 507, 521), so saving this again would count it twice.

59	it is calculated (through RisktRAC).  However, everyone should note that the 
60	credit department also receives our information.  Market risk and credit risk 
61	are inherently different, with different requirements.  This memo serves as a 
62	reminder of what some of the key differences are, how the credit system uses 
63	RisktRAC differently from market risk, how this affects us, what some key 
64	problems are in the credit system caused by our data, and changes to be made

76	Market risk picks up all officialized books.  If a book is not officialized 
77	it does not pick the book up.
78	Credit picks up all officalized books.  If a book is not officialized, it 
79	picks up the previous day's position.  Therefore, if positions in book A are 
80	moved to book B, and A is no longer officialized, credit picks up the 
81	previous day's position for book A.  As a result, if a book is no longer 
82	used, please officialize it the first day it is no longer used, so credit 
83	will pick up 0 on a go forward basis.

86	counterparty information has deteriorated.  Enron official counterparty names 
87	need to be used so they flow properly to credit.

90	As referenced above: correct counterparty names and books with 0 positions

content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is item 6 of 10 in decisions.md, at 39 minutes once a month, which comes to 0.65 hours or $55.25 a month. The idea is sound, but I rewrote parts of your draft before saving because some claims didn't match the mail.

**What I corrected:**
- **Unsupported claim:** "Four or more people then spent weeks finding and fixing it" isn't in 175.eml. That message only shows Joanie Ngo asking on 4/16 for the March deal 640685 to be confirmed and rebooked, because it had been copied from January's deal 547201. Nothing shows weeks of work by four people, so I cut it.
- **Better evidence, which you hadn't cited:** In 83.eml (Megan Parker, 8/7/2001), Julie Meyers did January and February "but March forward was never completed." It also says "Julie zeroed this out, but O'Neal put it back," and Parker then lists what must be done by hand to finish March, April and May. This shows how the monthly hand steps actually failed.
- **Proof the work kept going:** 28.eml (10/30/2001) shows the work still running in October. Parker had "sent an email to risk to update the demand fees for the prior months and to book Aug and Sept crude." 72.eml also asks where the July deal is. So the work is ongoing and the monthly rate is fair. I used 28.eml as an occurrence in place of 30.eml, which is a cost question rather than the ticket work.

**The estimate:** I kept your 39 minutes a month. It is cautious, because the catch-up in August to October looks bigger than your amortised 12 minutes of rework. The stated rate is "This needs to be done monthly prior to flash" (175.eml). `check` confirmed all quotes, including the ones from the encoded 83.eml.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Not in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md lines 82 and 103 mention it.)

TITLE: Replace the hand-run "official post id" macro and the controllers' nightly verification sheet with a system-generated end-of-night list of every assigned post ID not yet marked official (including flat/zero-position ones), sent automatically to each book admin and controller before they leave

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Every night each book admin must mark every book and post ID official in the risk system, including books with no position, because credit otherwise picks up yesterday's position. Missed books land on a daily exception list that goes to Sally Beck and is reviewed weekly by Rick Buy. To avoid that, desks built their own Excel macro, which someone must run by hand each night after typing in the date and book codes. Controllers also get a verification sheet each night. The existing position-based control misses post IDs with no net position.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/595.eml (Moscoso, 10/16/2000): "We have been tracking books that are not officialized on a daily basis.  This list goes to Sally Beck and is reviewed at the end of each week by Rick Buy." / "It is imperative that we take extra care to ensure that all books are marked official each night before going home.  A control process should be implemented immediately". Then: "Darron Giron didn't officialize the West-NW-GDL book on Friday." Giron's reply: "The reason my mistake was not caught on the benchmark signoff procedure is that the postid in question did not have a net position." / "If a postid has a net position and is not officialized, it will be caught using this procedure.  It will not, however, if the postid does not have a position."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/590.eml: "We are currently looking into a query which will allow us to see all of our officialized books each night.  It is not ready now, but should be soon."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/582.eml (Dutch Quigley's macro, forwarded to 5 book admins): "The macro in this file will query all official books for given Portfolio and Book codes.  Use it to make sure all your postid's that need to be, are officialized each night." / "To run this file all that has to be done is enter the date and have the Portfolio and Book CD entered in also."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/580.eml (Greg Couch / Kam Keiser modification): "This one requires a comment in all post-id's to pull in only those."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/533.eml (Giron to 5 admins, 11/2/2000): "Let's make sure we are doing this every night.  I think Jason has been running the official post id macro most nights, but we need to have the last person finished do it every day." Gossett to Sally Beck: "1. Each book adm. now checks his/her own positions that are going into V@R" / "2. All regional controllers will receive a sheet at the end of the night, verifying that all books are officialized."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/401.eml (Shona Wilson, 12/11/2000): "when a book is flat it still has an effect on credit.  Flat books must be officialized" / "If a book is not officialized, it picks up the previous day's position."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/492.eml lists 20 Enovate/EMW post IDs "that are officialized each night" for one desk alone.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
The risk system (or a scheduled job against it) holds the list of active post IDs per book admin. At a set time each evening it emails each admin and their regional controller the post IDs not yet marked official, including zero-position ones, and repeats until the list is empty. This replaces the hand-run macro, the hand-built verification sheet, and the next-morning exception chase.

AFTERWARDS
Nobody types dates and book codes into a macro. The controller's sheet is generated automatically. Flat books aren't missed, so there are no Beck/Buy exception-list incidents and no email chains about them.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: nightly ("each night", 582/595/492; "every night ... every day", 533). About 21 business days a month.
- Minutes per night today, West desk only: the last admin opens the macro, enters the date and codes, runs it and checks the results, ~5; the regional controller reviews the verification sheet, ~3. That's 8 min.
- Afterwards: reading an automatic email with an empty or short list takes about 1 min. Saved ≈ 7 min a night.
- Missed-book incidents: the 10/16/2000 one involved Moscoso, Gossett and Giron writing explanations (595, 590), about 30 min combined. I count one incident a quarter, ≈ 10 min a month.
- 21 × 7 + 10 = 157 min ≈ 2.6 hours/month × $85 ≈ $222/month for one regional desk. Gossett's 533 note shows the same control at every desk (Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Baumbach and McLaughlin got the macro in 582). I haven't multiplied by desks because the minutes there aren't shown.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

56	Subject: How do officialized books make it to credit?
57	
58	In the past few months much focus has been put on understanding VAR and how 
59	it is calculated (through RisktRAC).  However, everyone should note that the 
60	credit department also receives our information.  Market risk and credit risk 
61	are inherently different, with different requirements.  This memo serves as a 
62	reminder of what some of the key differences are, how the credit system uses 
63	RisktRAC differently from market risk, how this affects us, what some key 
64	problems are in the credit system caused by our data, and changes to be made 
65	by risk management groups.
66	
67	differences are between credit and market risk - you all know this, but many 
68	of your ba's don't. 
69	when a book is flat it still has an effect on credit.  Flat books must be 
70	officialized
71	market risk is keyed off positions and curves.  When we make money, market 
72	risk is reduced.  Credit risk is keyed off positions with customers.  When we 
73	make money, credit risk is increased, as people owe us more money.
74	
75	how the credit system uses RisktRAC differently from market risk
76	Market risk picks up all officialized books.  If a book is not officialized 
77	it does not pick the book up.
78	Credit picks up all officalized books.  If a book is not officialized, it 
79	picks up the previous day's position.  Therefore, if positions in book A are 
80	moved to book B, and A is no longer officialized, credit picks up the 
81	previous day's position for book A.  As a result, if a book is no longer 
82	used, please officialize it the first day it is no longer used, so credit 
83	will pick up 0 on a go forward basis.
84	Market risk is not concerned with counterparty codes and names.
85	Credit needs correct counterparty codes and names.  In recent months, the 
86	counterparty information has deteriorated.  Enron official counterparty names 
87	need to be used so they flow properly to credit.
88	
89	what are some key problems in the credit system caused by our data
90	As referenced above: correct counterparty names and books with 0 positions 
91	not being officialized so credit picks up previous day info.
92	As a takeaway from this message please ensure only correct counterparty names 
93	are used and that if a book has 0 positions that it is officialized the first 
94	day it has 0 positions.
95	
96	If you have specific questions about credit, please call Debbie Brackett, at 
97	X35856. 
98	
99	
100

TITLE: Stop the monthly email request to Risk to reprice EnerVest Sitara deal S#27239. Either give the deal a formula/actual-invoice price type that Settlements actualizes when the invoice arrives, or give the Settlements analyst rights to update the price on this deal.

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each production month, the EnerVest invoice carries a calculated price (to six decimal places). The Settlements analyst (Tricia Truong) emails the West desk risk lead (Darron Giron, earlier Dawn Kenne) asking him to change the rate on S#27239 to that number. He changes it by hand and replies "Done". The requests are sometimes held up for weeks, need reminders and escalation, and get passed on when the owner changes.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/301.eml (1/23/2001): "As usual, could you please change rate on S# 27239 for 12/00 production to $5.811329?" Reply: "Done".
- corpus/giron-d/sent/378.eml (12/20/2000): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.15544 for Nov. 00 Production ?" Reply: "Done".
- corpus/giron-d/sent/469.eml (11/21/2000): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.878216 for Oct. 00 production?" Reply: "Done.  I did the 1999 changes as well."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/508.eml (10/11 to 11/13/2000): "I've already received invoice for 9/00 production.  Could you please change its price to 4.417791 (S#27239)?" Dawn Kenne: "Darron, this is that wonderful Enervest issue." Bryce Baxter chase: "Darron - have you had a chance to take a look at this yet?" Giron: "It's done.  I appologize for this taking so long.  It won't happen again."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/313.eml (1/9 to 1/19/2001): "Could you please change rate on the above deal from $2.24246 to $2.156695 for days 2/21/00 - 2/29/00?" Then "This is just a friendly reminder....." Giron: "Done.  Sorry it took so long."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/141.eml (3/20/2001): "Could you please help me change the rate for the above Sitara # for Jan. 01 production to $9.624065?  Please let me know if you're no longer handling this." Giron: "Please send these to Kristen Clause in the future."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Set S#27239's price type so the monthly price comes from the EnerVest invoice/statement, entered once by Settlements as part of actualizing the month, as is done for other invoice-priced deals. If the contract formula is known, encode it so Sitara calculates it. In both cases no request goes to Risk.

AFTERWARDS
Settlements enters the invoiced price once when it processes the invoice, which it already handles. There are no emails, no reminders, no hand-offs when the risk lead changes, and no weeks of delay holding up payment.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly. "As usual" (301), and requests appear for Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec 2000 and Jan 2001 production (508, 469, 378, 301, 141), plus prior-period corrections (313, and the 1999 changes in 469).
- Minutes today per month: Truong writes the request ~3; Giron opens the deal, changes the price and replies ~6. Reminders and escalation in about 2 of 6 months (508: Truong follow-ups, Kenne hand-off, Baxter chase; 313: reminder) ≈ 15 min each, averaging ≈ 5 min a month. Total ≈ 14 min.
- Afterwards: Settlements types the price into the deal while actualizing, ~3 min (this time moves to Settlements and is netted out).
- Saved ≈ 11 min/month ≈ 0.18 hours × $85 ≈ $16/month. It's small, but it's a pure removal of a hand-off for one deal. The same pattern (settlements asking risk to reprice invoice-priced deals monthly) is also in farmer-d (e.g. the Peoples/North Shore demand charges), but I don't count it here.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

3	  "today": "HPL sells gas to the Texas General Land Office (GLO) and Enron Gas Marketing (EGM) receives crude in exchange. In March 2001 Bryce Baxter set up a four-ticket accounting treatment that has to be redone by hand every month before flash. Someone zeroes the price on that month's HPL sale to GLO. They work out the gas value (index x firm volume) and enter it as demand charges on the HPL-to-ENA and ENA-Wellhead tickets. They enter the prior month's crude value on the ENA-to-EGM demand ticket. Julie Meyers did this for January and February 2001, but the March deal was copied from January's with the price still on it, and March onward was never completed. A price she had zeroed was also put back. By August and October 2001, Megan Parker was rebuilding March to May by hand and asking Risk to update demand fees for prior months and book August and September crude.",
