2	  "name": "Requests to extend expired deals at flowing meters",
3	  "today": "Gas keeps flowing at a meter after its Sitara deal ends, or on days the deal does not cover. The allocator (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Mary Poorman and others) finds it on the allocation exception screen or a feedback-error list after the month, parks the gas on Strangers Gas, and emails Daren Farmer about that one meter. Daren checks with the trader or contract admin and extends the deal or enters a new one; only then can accounting build an accounting arrangement and the allocator reallocate. Many volumes are tiny, the same meters come back month after month, and threads stall when the person who owns the deal is out or on another desk.",
4	  "change": "Warn the desk before month-end about deals ending at meters that still flow, and roll steady meters and tiny overflow volumes forward by rule instead of by email.",
5	  "explanation": "A list run before month-end matches meters with recent flow against Sitara deals that end that month, so Daren or the trader can extend or end each deal before the allocator finds the gap. Deals at meters that flow every month are entered as evergreen when the contract allows it, with the evergreen flag checked against the contract term at entry. Volumes under a small tolerance on days just past a deal's end attach to the prior deal by a rule the desk agrees in advance. Allocators then email Daren only about real renegotiations or contract questions, such as the Duke deal at meter 5892.",

TITLE: Automate the nightly EPE reconciliation (Real Time El Paso model vs. CARP report) so a query compares the two and records "no variance" itself, and the night trader only investigates the flagged variances

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
In July 2001 Real Time Trading Support (Kate Symes) built an "EPE Reconciliation Model", a spreadsheet on the shared drive. The Portland real-time night shift must fill in a daily entry comparing the Real Time El Paso model with the CARP report. They must do this even when nothing differs, because Houston (Settlements/Volume Management: Thresa Allen, Amy Clemons, Virginia Thompson) reads a blank sheet as "CARP was not run". In the first 8 days nothing differed, yet the shift still has to fill it in every night, and a missed night has already led to a reprimand email.
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/418.eml (Kate Symes, 9 Jul 2001, to Thresa Allen and Amy Clemons, cc Virginia Thompson and Bill Williams III): "I wanted to quickly follow-up to make sure everyone is aware of the new EPE Reconciliation Model's location and status. I just skimmed through the first 8 days of this month, and we show no variances between the Real Time El Paso model and our CARP report." / "m:/Electric/Epe/Epe01/July01/July EPE Reconciliation"
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/417.eml (Bill Williams III, 10 Jul 2001, to David Porter and Mark Guzman): "Great job on the cong last night but the EPE reconciliation sheet was not done.  Even if there are no variances, please complete the July EPE Reconciliation sheet going forward.  Houston will assume that no one ran the CARP if the sheet has no entries."
- The file is set up per month (Epe01/July01), so it is rebuilt or copied each month.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
A scheduled job (or a macro triggered when CARP finishes) pulls the night's CARP output and the Real Time El Paso model figures. It compares them hour by hour, writes the result to the reconciliation file (including an automatic "no variance – CARP run at hh:mm" stamp), and emails the shift and Houston only when there is a variance. The monthly file is generated automatically.

AFTERWARDS
On no-variance nights (8 of 8 in the first week of July), nobody touches the sheet, and Houston still sees proof that CARP ran. On variance nights the trader starts from a list of the differing hours instead of keying both sides in. There are no reprimand emails for blank sheets.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: nightly ("Even if there are no variances, please complete ... going forward"; Kate's check covered "the first 8 days of this month", one entry per day). The real-time desk works every day, so about 30 a month.
- Minutes per night today: open the monthly sheet, pull the CARP and El Paso model numbers and enter or compare them, mark the result ≈ 10 min. That's my estimate; the mail does not state the time.
- Afterwards: about 0 on no-variance nights, plus a little more on variance nights. Net saved ≈ 8 min a night.
- 30 × 8 = 240 min = 4.0 hours/month × $85 = $340/month (≈ $4,080/yr). The one-time build cost is not counted.

content.text: These are one-off narrative notes and hard to estimate, so I'm skipping them. Next I'm checking the intercompany HPLC/ENA variance work.

I saved the proposal. It is item 5 of 14 in decisions.md, at $184.45 a month (6 minutes × 21.67 working days a month = 2.17 hours). Nothing in decisions.md covered this work before. All the quotes are in the mail, and the nightly rate is stated outright in 533.eml ("Let's make sure we are doing this every night.").

I made these changes before saving:

- **Wrong name:** You wrote that Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Baumbach and McLaughlin got the macro in 582. Dutch Quigley actually sent it to Gossett, Baumbach, Kelly, **Giron** and Keiser. McLaughlin only appears in 401, as someone Gossett forwarded the credit memo to. I dropped that claim.
- **"Hand-built verification sheet":** 533 only says controllers "will receive a sheet at the end of the night". It doesn't say who makes it or how. I described it as a separate sheet that the new report would replace, not as hand-built.
- **Minutes, 6 instead of your 7 + incidents:** The macro already does the query, so running it is only a few minutes. Admins and controllers would still have to read the new email and act on it. The mail shows only one missed-book incident, the 10/16/2000 one, so "one a quarter" is a guess. I kept it to about half a minute a night. The total of 6 minutes a night for the West desk is about the same as your figure.
- **Quotes and how often:** I used 533 (twice) and 582 as the evidence that the work happens, and kept your quotes from 580, 595, 401 and 492 as evidence. The `check` tool found only 2 dated occurrences, which works out to 0.5 a month, so the saving rests on the stated nightly rate. That rate is supported by 533, 582 and 492.
- **Not multiplied across desks:** I agree with you on this. The mail doesn't show the minutes at the other desks.

Tom, we attached both a consolidated p&l and an updated prudency schedule. 
The weater hedge made $165,000 today.  The only odd thing that we saw was the 
physical change due to deal changes with the HPLC Operational desk. This desk 
is a desk that is set up to account for fuel, gas loss, and physical UA4, we 
have tickets out there with zero volumes on them that get updated after the 
month is over once volume management knows where the gas needs to be 
allocated. What we found out that happened was that in the last week of 
February and in the first week of March Sitara added volumes to these tickets 
before were were running comparison reports to see the changes.  Darren 
noticed the incorrect volumes on these tickets and had logistics zero them 
out.  Darren thought that the changes would have no position effect as if it 
were a deal between HPLC and Texas, but it is actuall as if we changed a deal 
that we did with another region.  The value was offset by changes in TUFCO 
and storage.  We released $270,000 out of March prudency to keep you flat for 
the day.  Hope you had fun at the school function. I'll be here until about 
8:30, so feel free to call if you get this.
Bryan

91	We are positioning ourselves to release a new Product Type that we will refer 
92	to as a Flexible Physical Gas product. Legal is in the process of drafting a 
93	GTC and Product Type description that will be used with this Product Type. I 
94	will start the building process once Legal provides the GTC and Product Type 
95	description; but in the interim, here's a broadstroke description of how the 
96	transaction works:
97	
98	Party A and Party B exchange gas during the month of June 2000.
99	
100	Party A buys 10,000 MMBtu per day (or 300,000 total MMBtu) at TCO Pool Index
101	
102	Party B has the right to notify Party A of when Party B wants to take 
103	delivery during the month of June, and may take delivery in one of three 
104	forms: 3-day delivery, 5-day delivery, or 10-day delivery. The gas nominated 
105	for each such day would be a percentage of the total 300,000 MMBtu (i.e.; If 
106	Party B chooses 5 days for nomination, Party A would deliver 20% of the 
107	300,000 MMBtu on each of those 5 days for a total nom of 100%).  Party B pay 
108	TCO Pool Index PLUS a premium.
109	
110	I understand that this type of transaction is currently done 
111	over-the-counter. Scott Mills has previously issued an explanatory e-mail of 
112	Sitara concerns and we should begin to address those issues.
113	
114	Bjorn - if you could ask someone to prepare a Sigma Factor in advance, then 
115	my turn around time to for the Product Type should be reduced. Also, due to 
116	the varying 'optionality', do you think these three different products will 
117	require three different Product Types?
118	
119	Please feel free to call if you have any questions.
120

cc: Scott Hendrickson/HOU/ECT@ECT

to as a Flexible Physical Gas product. Legal is in the process of drafting a 
GTC and Product Type description that will be used with this Product Type. I 
will start the building process once Legal provides the GTC and Product Type 
description; but in the interim, here's a broadstroke description of how the 
transaction works:

Party A and Party B exchange gas during the month of June 2000.

Party A buys 10,000 MMBtu per day (or 300,000 total MMBtu) at TCO Pool Index

Party B has the right to notify Party A of when Party B wants to take 
delivery during the month of June, and may take delivery in one of three 
forms: 3-day delivery, 5-day delivery, or 10-day delivery. The gas nominated 
for each such day would be a percentage of the total 300,000 MMBtu (i.e.; If 
Party B chooses 5 days for nomination, Party A would deliver 20% of the 
300,000 MMBtu on each of those 5 days for a total nom of 100%).  Party B pay 
TCO Pool Index PLUS a premium.

over-the-counter. Scott Mills has previously issued an explanatory e-mail of 
Sitara concerns and we should begin to address those issues.

my turn around time to for the Product Type should be reduced. Also, due to 
the varying 'optionality', do you think these three different products will 
require three different Product Types?

Please feel free to call if you have any questions.

Dale

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Nothing on intercompany variances in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md line 15 mentions it.)

TITLE: Have Sitara create the mirror side of every HPLC↔ENA intercompany deal automatically, and add a daily intercompany nomination tie-out, so missing or mismatched sides are caught before month-end accrual instead of being researched by Settlements afterwards

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
HPLC and ENA trade with each other through pairs of Sitara deals entered separately on each side. Often one side isn't entered, or the volumes on the two sides differ. Texas Gas Settlements finds this only when the month-end accrual or the intercompany report doesn't tie. It then emails logistics and the desk one deal at a time to research the gap, and has to clear everything by month-end.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/868.eml (Gregg Lenart, Texas Gas Settlements, "FEB2000 Intercompany Accrual variances", to Csikos, Clynes, Wynne, Nelson, Farmer, White): "Below is a list of Sitara deals that had volume variances or where one side (purchase/sale) did not get accrued for the FEB 2000 accrual." / "since Intercompany Sitara deals are the same that the nominations on both sides should match on the month end accruals." Lists 7 deals "Missing on Purchase side (ENA)" totalling "1,395,689mmbtu $3,710,497.72" plus one volume variance of "24,167mmbtu  <$60,538.34>". / "MISSION:     Proactively Identify and resolve Intercompany volume issues upstream." / "Third Goal:  Minimizing analyse time saving $$$$."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/877.eml (Thu Nguyen, 2/17 and 3/3/2000): "I have an intercompany deal which I am missing one side of.  HPL purchased gas from Dynegy (deal 96378) and sold to ENA (deal97185) on Oasis Pipeline (meter 1335).   I can't find ENA's purchase from HPL." / "This is affecting our intercompany report and we need to have it cleaned as soon as possible." Two weeks later: "Have you a chance to look into this?  We are required to clear intercompany variances by the end of the month".

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) When an HPLC↔ENA deal is entered in Sitara, the counterparty-side ticket is generated automatically from the same terms, so there's a single entry and no missing side. (2) A daily report compares nominations on both sides of each intercompany pair and sends any differences to the scheduler that day, while the gas month is still open.

AFTERWARDS
Missing-side items (7 of the 8 on Lenart's February list) can't happen. Volume differences show up daily for the scheduler to fix in the normal course. Settlements no longer builds a month-end variance list or chases logistics deal by deal.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly. Intercompany variances must be cleared each month ("We are required to clear intercompany variances by the end of the month", 877), and the list is built per accrual month ("FEB2000 Intercompany Accrual variances", 868).
- Items per month: 8 on the February 2000 list (868). I use 6 to be conservative.
- Minutes per item today: Settlements finds the item and writes it up ~5; the scheduler/desk researches it (where the other side went, which deal) and fixes or enters it ~15; follow-up as in 877 ~5. About 25 min.
- Afterwards: missing sides are gone. A small volume difference is fixed the same day by the scheduler in ~5 min. Saved ≈ 20 min per item.
- 6 × 20 = 120 min = 2.0 hours/month × $85 = $170/month (≈ $2,040/yr). This doesn't count the P&L and accrual error, which was $3.7M of unaccrued purchases in one month.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

content.text: EPE reconciliation is already saved, so my pending version will likely come back as a duplicate. Next I'm looking at the MIPS zero-volume overrides lead.

I saved the proposal as item 4 of 16 in decisions.md, after making some corrections. It now comes to **5 minutes × 30.42 times a month = 2.54 hours = $215.90 a month**, down from the analyst's $340 a month. No other critic had saved or rejected the same work.

The saved file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-3\proposals\epe-nightly-reconciliation.json`.

**What the mail supports:** 418.eml and 417.eml say what the analyst quoted. I also found more evidence:
- **304.eml (14 Aug 2001):** Kate Symes's list of reminders, which she sent to Bill Williams to check before sending to the traders. It says "El Paso model must tie out with CARP when trading day is done" and "El Paso totals should be logged in the reconciliation model (…/aug01/…) and all variances explained." This shows the work was still going on in August, and it gives the daily frequency.
- **315.eml (8 Aug 2001):** The July month-end checkout with Settlements "took approximately five minutes, as opposed to the five days we spent sorting it out last month."

**What I corrected:**
1. **Minutes cut from 8 to 5 a night.** 315.eml shows the reconciliation already works well, so the only saving is the nightly entry: logging the totals and checking the tie-out. The trader still has to explain any variances. Five minutes is a realistic figure for that.
2. **Unsupported claims removed:**
   - The mail does not say Kate built the model, only that it was "new".
   - The Houston people's team names are not in the mail.
   - "Keying both sides in" is not shown anywhere.
   - "Reprimand" overstates Bill's note. It begins "Great job on the cong last night" before asking for the sheet, so I call it a reminder.
3. **Stated rate set to once a day, quoting 304.eml.** The analyst's quote, "going forward", says the work continues but not how often. The real-time desk works every day, so "per day" fits. Counting the dated messages alone would give only about once a month, so the saving depends on this stated daily rate.
4. **315.eml added as evidence** so managers can see the claim covers only the nightly entry, not the month-end checkout.

The analyst's note found no text in the mail that tried to instruct an automated processor, and neither did I.

In reviewing some of the imbalance numbers, I discovered that Valero Texoma 
(#71) BAV volumes have not fed into POPS since 3/14 causing an out of balance 
at the meter in excess of 500,000mm month to date.  The more critical part of 
this problem, however, is that POPS has fed 0 volumes back to Sitara on some 
of the HPLC deals.  This means that these purchase volumes (expenses) have 
not been picked up in Tom's P&L and are, instead, sitting in UA4.  To the 
extent that the purchase prices vary from the UA4 value, the P&L may take a 
hit when these actual volumes flow through.

I realize that Kim is out and that you guys are stretched thin, however, a 
problem of this magnitude needs to be addressed as soon as it's discovered.  
Someone needs to be overriding the 0 volumes so that Sitara is receiving 
correct information and the P&L is kept as accurate as possible.

Please give me a call if you have any questions.

In reviewing some of the imbalance numbers, I discovered that Valero Texoma 
(#71) BAV volumes have not fed into POPS since 3/14 causing an out of balance 
at the meter in excess of 500,000mm month to date.  The more critical part of 
this problem, however, is that POPS has fed 0 volumes back to Sitara on some 
of the HPLC deals.  This means that these purchase volumes (expenses) have 
not been picked up in Tom's P&L and are, instead, sitting in UA4.  To the 
extent that the purchase prices vary from the UA4 value, the P&L may take a 
hit when these actual volumes flow through.

I realize that Kim is out and that you guys are stretched thin, however, a 
problem of this magnitude needs to be addressed as soon as it's discovered.  
Someone needs to be overriding the 0 volumes so that Sitara is receiving 
correct information and the P&L is kept as accurate as possible.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in decisions.md. The main problem is the idea itself. The evidence for the payoff is also thin.

**1. The fix targets the wrong cause.** The proposal assumes each side of an HPLC↔ENA deal is entered as a separate Sitara deal, so one side can go missing. Lenart's email (868) says otherwise: "since Intercompany Sitara deals are the same that the nominations on both sides should match on the month end accruals." His list gives one Sitara number per item, and the ENA purchase side of that same deal "did not get accrued." What's missing is the ENA side's nomination and accrual, not a deal ticket. He also asks whether there is a "system limitation," which suggests he doesn't know why that side drops out. Having Sitara create mirror tickets automatically would not stop it. So the claim that "missing-side items (7 of the 8) can't happen" doesn't hold.

877 doesn't support a two-ticket setup either. The two deals there are HPL's purchase from Dynegy and HPL's sale to ENA. The thing Thu can't find is "ENA's purchase from HPL," which fits a missing ENA-side nomination.

**2. Other variances in the mail have different causes.** The June 2000 cleanup list (1185–1187, "Interconnect / Intercompany issues") lists desk-to-desk variances caused by:
- custody transfer: Tetco's volume against HPL Measurement's
- a third party invoicing the entire flow at Carthage (Devon)
- swing-meter actuals that don't match PGEV's allocations
- pipeline nominations out of balance at Transco Meter 74

Neither part of the proposed change would fix these.

**3. Frequency and savings are mostly assumed.** There is one month's list (Feb 2000, 868) and one older item (July 99, 877). The "clear by the end of the month" quote supports a monthly deadline, but the 6 items a month is a guess from that single list. The savings would be only 2 hours a month ($170), and the main idea doesn't hold. The $3.7M figure is purchases that went unaccrued for one month, not time saved, and shouldn't be cited as a saving.

**What could fix it:** Drop the mirror-ticket idea and rebuild the proposal around the daily nomination tie-out, which is a reasonable idea. To support it, look for:
- mail explaining how the ENA side of an intercompany Sitara deal gets nominated and why it goes missing (the "system limitation" in 868)
- variance lists for other months, to show how many items come up each month

The tie-out would also need to treat measurement differences (like those in 1187) separately from missing nominations.

No other critic had saved or rejected anything on intercompany variances.

input.prompt:
Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Nothing on MIPS/POPS zero volumes in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md line 28 mentions it.)

TITLE: Change the nightly MIPS→POPS file so "no data yet / incomplete" is sent as an incomplete flag instead of a zero (the fix measurement's software vendor already identified). Schedulers then stop overriding POPS zeros with Gas Control estimates by hand and re-doing it after each nightly roll.

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
For outside-measured and mirrored/bidirectional meters, measurement (MIPS) has no volume until month-end. So every night it sends POPS a zero preliminary. That zero becomes the "best available" number and overwrites Gas Control's estimate. It then flows into Sitara and the desk P&L, leaving purchase expense sitting in UA4. Pipeline Operations schedulers have to spot these zeros and type the estimates back into POPS. The next nightly roll can write zeros over them again. Measurement called the fix "not a priority", and management escalated.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/928.eml (Charlotte Hawkins, 3/21/2000): "We do have a problem with some of our mirrored meters.  When MIPS receives an \"incomplete\" from the parent meter it sends a -0- to POPS.  Yes, this is a big problem.  Our POPS team (Romeo D'Souza) has identified this problem and notified MIPS.  However, he was told this was not a priority item.   In the mean time we are overriding the volumes in POPS with the estimated volumes." / "the 14th rolled last night from MIPS and overrode the BAV with a -0- from day 14 forward." / "This was corrected this morning and the meter re-allocated."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/925.eml (Lauri Allen): "POPS has fed 0 volumes back to Sitara on some of the HPLC deals.  This means that these purchase volumes (expenses) have not been picked up in Tom's P&L and are, instead, sitting in UA4." / "Someone needs to be overriding the 0 volumes so that Sitara is receiving correct information"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/936.eml (Michael Eiben): "We continue to have this problem at various bidirectional meters and meter 980071 below is the latest casuality.  When MIPS sends Pipeline Operations a zero prelim, this becomes the best available number and overlays the estimate that Gas Control sends us.  When this happens & scheduling doesn't catch to override the zero, the desk's expense is understated. This is causing a huge mess for Texas Operations." Gary Anderson (measurement): "This is an outside measured volume that we don't receive volumes on until month's end so systematically, no information equals zero." / "The only possible solution is to tag all zero volumes sent in the nightly file process as (i) incomplete." Charlotte Hawkins: "the on-going problem of MIPS feeding zeros to POPS when incomplete data is received."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1013.eml (Robert Lloyd, 4/4/2000, another meter, Enron Methanol 988291): "Please override POP'S  daily volume{ presently zero}  to reflect  daily activity you can obtain from Gas Control." / "This change is needed  ASAP for economics purposes."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
MIPS sends zero-with-no-data as an "incomplete" flag in the nightly file, as Anderson proposed. POPS keeps the Gas Control estimate as best-available until a real measured volume arrives. No hand overrides are needed, and the nightly roll doesn't undo them.

AFTERWARDS
Schedulers don't hunt for zeroed meters or retype estimates every morning. The P&L and UA4 aren't distorted mid-month, and there are no escalation threads.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: nightly. The MIPS file runs every night ("the 14th rolled last night from MIPS", "the nightly file process"), and for outside-measured meters "no information equals zero" until month-end. So the zeros come back every business day for the affected meters, across "various bidirectional meters".
- Minutes per business day today: a scheduler checks the affected meters for zeros, gets Gas Control's estimates, overrides POPS and re-allocates (928: "corrected this morning and the meter re-allocated"). About 10 min a day, conservatively, across the few meters involved.
- Escalation incidents (925/928/936 on 3/21 involved Allen, Hawkins, Eiben, Anderson and Lloyd; 1013 on 4/4): about 45 min of combined time each, at about 1 a month.
- 21 × 10 + 45 = 255 min ≈ 4.25 hours/month × $85 ≈ $361/month (≈ $4,300/yr). This doesn't count the P&L misstatement while zeros sit in UA4.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Schedulers don't hunt for zeroed meters or retype estimates every morning. The P&L and UA4 aren't distorted mid-month, and there are no escalation threads.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: nightly. The MIPS file runs every night ("the 14th rolled last night from MIPS", "the nightly file process"), and for outside-measured meters "no information equals zero" until month-end. So the zeros come back every business day for the affected meters, across "various bidirectional meters".
- Minutes per business day today: a scheduler checks the affected meters for zeros, gets Gas Control's estimates, overrides POPS and re-allocates (928: "corrected this morning and the meter re-allocated"). About 10 min a day, conservatively, across the few meters involved.
- Escalation incidents (925/928/936 on 3/21 involved Allen, Hawkins, Eiben, Anderson and Lloyd; 1013 on 4/4): about 45 min of combined time each, at about 1 a month.
- 21 × 10 + 45 = 255 min ≈ 4.25 hours/month × $85 ≈ $361/month (≈ $4,300/yr). This doesn't count the P&L misstatement while zeros sit in UA4.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Nothing on volumetric explanations in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md lines 56 and 89 mention it.)

TITLE: Pre-fill the monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations in the Statistical Database with each region's previous explanation, and ask controllers to respond only where a variance crosses ±10% for a new reason, instead of a fresh email write-up from every regional risk controller every month

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each month Business Analysis & Reporting (Misti Day) emails about 11 regional risk controllers and leads, copying the trading heads. She asks each of them to review the region's volumes in the "Statistical Database" and email back explanations for every ±10% change year/year, quarter/quarter and month/month, verified with commercial staff. The answers repeat month to month. Texas gave the same drivers in June and September.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1416.eml (Misti Day, 9/18/2000, "Wholesale Volumes - August", To: Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Baumbach, Confer, Leschber, Anderson; cc Harris, Killen, Shively, Neal, Allen): "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations!" / "Investor Relations requests that Business Analysis & Reporting provide monthly volumetric analysis for Wholesale Operations in addition to the quarterly analysis.  Please review the analysis for August 2000 and provide explanations for all material changes (+/- 10%) for the year/year, quarter/quarter, and month/month variances." / "It is essential that the volumes be verified by commercial personnel." / "Please forward your verification and explanations via e-mail to me by 10:00am Friday, September 22." Baumbach's reply: "Yr to Yr and Qtr to Qtr changes due to EOL and increased Entex takes."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml (same request for May 2000, 6/15/2000): "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations!" Baumbach's reply: "The Yr. to Yr. and Qtr to Qtr increases can be explained by an increase in EOL transactions and Entex taking more gas.  The Mo. to Mo. increase is attributable to increase EOL transactions and TUFCO taking more gas."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
The Statistical Database shows, next to each ±10% variance, the region's explanation from the prior month for the same comparison. The controller ticks "same driver" or types a new one directly in the database. No email request and reply cycle is needed, and BA&R doesn't have to collect and retype replies from emails. Commercial verification is needed only for new or changed explanations.

AFTERWARDS
For regions where the drivers persist (Texas: EOL growth, Entex and TUFCO takes), the monthly task is a quick confirmation. BA&R pulls the explanations straight from the database for Investor Relations.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly ("monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations", "provide monthly volumetric analysis ... in addition to the quarterly analysis", 1416/1210).
- People: about 11 regional controllers per round (1416 To: list). Plus Misti Day collecting and consolidating the replies.
- Minutes today per controller: review three comparisons in the database, check with a commercial person, and write the email ≈ 15. With pre-filled explanations, confirming persistent drivers ≈ 5, so 10 saved. 11 × 10 = 110 min.
- BA&R consolidation: retyping or merging 11 email replies ≈ 20 min, mostly removed. Say 15 saved.
- Total ≈ 125 min ≈ 2.1 hours/month × $85 ≈ $177/month (≈ $2,125/yr).

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

TITLE: Pre-fill the monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations in the Statistical Database with each region's previous explanation, and ask controllers to respond only where a variance crosses ±10% for a new reason, instead of a fresh email write-up from every regional risk controller every month

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each month Business Analysis & Reporting (Misti Day) emails about 11 regional risk controllers and leads, copying the trading heads. She asks each of them to review the region's volumes in the "Statistical Database" and email back explanations for every ±10% change year/year, quarter/quarter and month/month, verified with commercial staff. The answers repeat month to month. Texas gave the same drivers in June and September.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1416.eml (Misti Day, 9/18/2000, "Wholesale Volumes - August", To: Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Baumbach, Confer, Leschber, Anderson; cc Harris, Killen, Shively, Neal, Allen): "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations!" / "Investor Relations requests that Business Analysis & Reporting provide monthly volumetric analysis for Wholesale Operations in addition to the quarterly analysis.  Please review the analysis for August 2000 and provide explanations for all material changes (+/- 10%) for the year/year, quarter/quarter, and month/month variances." / "It is essential that the volumes be verified by commercial personnel." / "Please forward your verification and explanations via e-mail to me by 10:00am Friday, September 22." Baumbach's reply: "Yr to Yr and Qtr to Qtr changes due to EOL and increased Entex takes."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml (same request for May 2000, 6/15/2000): "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations!" Baumbach's reply: "The Yr. to Yr. and Qtr to Qtr increases can be explained by an increase in EOL transactions and Entex taking more gas.  The Mo. to Mo. increase is attributable to increase EOL transactions and TUFCO taking more gas."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
The Statistical Database shows, next to each ±10% variance, the region's explanation from the prior month for the same comparison. The controller ticks "same driver" or types a new one directly in the database. No email request and reply cycle is needed, and BA&R doesn't have to collect and retype replies from emails. Commercial verification is needed only for new or changed explanations.

AFTERWARDS
For regions where the drivers persist (Texas: EOL growth, Entex and TUFCO takes), the monthly task is a quick confirmation. BA&R pulls the explanations straight from the database for Investor Relations.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly ("monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations", "provide monthly volumetric analysis ... in addition to the quarterly analysis", 1416/1210).
- People: about 11 regional controllers per round (1416 To: list). Plus Misti Day collecting and consolidating the replies.
- Minutes today per controller: review three comparisons in the database, check with a commercial person, and write the email ≈ 15. With pre-filled explanations, confirming persistent drivers ≈ 5, so 10 saved. 11 × 10 = 110 min.
- BA&R consolidation: retyping or merging 11 email replies ≈ 20 min, mostly removed. Say 15 saved.
- Total ≈ 125 min ≈ 2.1 hours/month × $85 ≈ $177/month (≈ $2,125/yr).

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Nothing on curve validation in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md line 138 mentions it.)

TITLE: Route monthly gas curve-validation questions straight to the curve's owning trader through a maintained curve-owner list, and drop or pre-explain derived curves (e.g. NGI-PGE/TOPOCK, which equals NGI-SOCAL), instead of passing every question through the risk controller and desk risk leads

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each month the curve-validation group (Jennifer Nguyen) reviews 10 gas curves and sends questions about the ones that moved. The questions go to the risk controller (Jeff Gossett), who forwards them to three desk risk leads (Giron, Love, Keiser). The lead has to work out which curve is theirs and ask the trader (Phillip Allen, Keith Holst), then relay the answer back. Answers that are too short are sent back for another round, which repeats the hops. The same derived curve gets flagged month after month.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/170.eml (January validation): Nguyen to Gossett 2/27/2001: "Before I send out the memo for January, I have a few questions about 3 curves that were reviewed this month." Gossett to Giron, Love and Keiser: "Please get responses for these back to Jennifer today." Giron 3/5: "Phillip Allen and Keith Holst indicated that the curve changes in question for Socal was simply due to a higher forward market."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/132.eml (February validation): Nguyen 3/13/2001 to Giron, Love, Keiser: "Hopefully these curves are covered between the three of you!  Attached are the 10 curves reviewed for the month of February." Chase on 3/21: "Can you or anyone in your group follow up on the curves below?" Giron: "NGI-PGE/TOPOCK is an internal curve used to value transport and is equal to NGI-SOCAL.  This curve will probably show up every month because the West Coast is very volitile."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/49.eml and 47.eml (March validation, 4/17 to 4/23/2001): Giron: "The market just traded higher in the West in general during the month of March compared to February." Nguyen pushes back: "However, we are looking for specific reasons as to why this is so." Giron: "I asked Keith Holst (trader) again.  His answer was the same.  There were more buyers than sellers in the West during March, hence the price was stronger."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) Curve validation keeps a curve→owning-trader list (with a desk risk lead as backup) and sends each month's questions straight to the owner. (2) Curves defined as equal to another curve (Topock = SoCal) are validated through their parent and not questioned separately. (3) The request states the level of detail expected (market drivers, not just "traded higher") up front, which avoids the re-ask round.

AFTERWARDS
The owning trader answers once, straight to curve validation. Gossett's forwarding, the three leads working out who owns which curve, and the relay and re-ask through Giron all go away.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly. There is a validation round for January, February and March 2001 (170, 132, 49/47), each "for the month", with a memo issued monthly ("Before I send out the memo for January/March").
- Minutes per month today, routing only (the trader's own answer time stays): Gossett reads and forwards ~3; three desk leads each read the request and work out ownership ~5 each = 15; the lead who owns it asks the trader and relays the answer ~10; the chase or re-ask round (in 2 of the 3 months: the 3/21 chase and the 4/23 re-ask) ~10 averaged = ~7; Nguyen's chasing ~3. That's about 38 min.
- Afterwards: Nguyen looks up the owner list ~2 min. Saved ≈ 36 min a month.
- 36 min ≈ 0.6 hours/month × $85 ≈ $51/month (≈ $610/yr). This covers only the gas curves on Gossett's desks. Other commodities are not counted.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

TITLE: Route monthly gas curve-validation questions straight to the curve's owning trader through a maintained curve-owner list, and drop or pre-explain derived curves (e.g. NGI-PGE/TOPOCK, which equals NGI-SOCAL), instead of passing every question through the risk controller and desk risk leads

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
Each month the curve-validation group (Jennifer Nguyen) reviews 10 gas curves and sends questions about the ones that moved. The questions go to the risk controller (Jeff Gossett), who forwards them to three desk risk leads (Giron, Love, Keiser). The lead has to work out which curve is theirs and ask the trader (Phillip Allen, Keith Holst), then relay the answer back. Answers that are too short are sent back for another round, which repeats the hops. The same derived curve gets flagged month after month.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/170.eml (January validation): Nguyen to Gossett 2/27/2001: "Before I send out the memo for January, I have a few questions about 3 curves that were reviewed this month." Gossett to Giron, Love and Keiser: "Please get responses for these back to Jennifer today." Giron 3/5: "Phillip Allen and Keith Holst indicated that the curve changes in question for Socal was simply due to a higher forward market."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/132.eml (February validation): Nguyen 3/13/2001 to Giron, Love, Keiser: "Hopefully these curves are covered between the three of you!  Attached are the 10 curves reviewed for the month of February." Chase on 3/21: "Can you or anyone in your group follow up on the curves below?" Giron: "NGI-PGE/TOPOCK is an internal curve used to value transport and is equal to NGI-SOCAL.  This curve will probably show up every month because the West Coast is very volitile."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/49.eml and 47.eml (March validation, 4/17 to 4/23/2001): Giron: "The market just traded higher in the West in general during the month of March compared to February." Nguyen pushes back: "However, we are looking for specific reasons as to why this is so." Giron: "I asked Keith Holst (trader) again.  His answer was the same.  There were more buyers than sellers in the West during March, hence the price was stronger."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
(1) Curve validation keeps a curve→owning-trader list (with a desk risk lead as backup) and sends each month's questions straight to the owner. (2) Curves defined as equal to another curve (Topock = SoCal) are validated through their parent and not questioned separately. (3) The request states the level of detail expected (market drivers, not just "traded higher") up front, which avoids the re-ask round.

AFTERWARDS
The owning trader answers once, straight to curve validation. Gossett's forwarding, the three leads working out who owns which curve, and the relay and re-ask through Giron all go away.

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly. There is a validation round for January, February and March 2001 (170, 132, 49/47), each "for the month", with a memo issued monthly ("Before I send out the memo for January/March").
- Minutes per month today, routing only (the trader's own answer time stays): Gossett reads and forwards ~3; three desk leads each read the request and work out ownership ~5 each = 15; the lead who owns it asks the trader and relays the answer ~10; the chase or re-ask round (in 2 of the 3 months: the 3/21 chase and the 4/23 re-ask) ~10 averaged = ~7; Nguyen's chasing ~3. That's about 38 min.
- Afterwards: Nguyen looks up the owner list ~2 min. Saved ≈ 36 min a month.
- 36 min ≈ 0.6 hours/month × $85 ≈ $51/month (≈ $610/yr). This covers only the gas curves on Gossett's desks. Other commodities are not counted.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

33:- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
34:- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
35:- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
38:- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word nomination with a structured feed into HPL scheduling that rolls forward and is sent only when volumes change.. Why: The 16 minutes a day rest on steps the mail does not show: a phone call every day (only 5 of about 23 nominations mention one), HPL retyping the Word file (no message shows it), and frequent no-change days (none shown; REVISED resends and monthly nominations show volumes change), and the 30-a-month rate ignores that weekend days come in one Friday email (1330.eml); three critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the schedulers (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) showing what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as retyping it into the system, keying errors, corrections or rework after revisions, and nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller saving counted once per working day.
41:- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off tiny Strangers Gas volumes under a standing approval and send the rest to Daren Farmer as one weekly electronic list instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 flows sent mostly in a burst from 11 Dec 2000 to 12 Jan 2001 and none appear after that, though the mailbox runs to late 2001; so the work is an episode that has ended, not 10 items a month, and the same work has already been rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, in this or other mailboxes (Cernosek, Lannou, Boas), that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
59:- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale as a standing zero-price ticket and price the HPL-to-ENA demand tickets by formula (firm volume x the month's index), so only the crude value is keyed monthly.. Why: The same change to the same work is already saved in decisions.md (item 7). This version also gets today's process wrong: the mail shows the monthly steps were not done at all from March 2001 on and had to be caught up months later, not keyed by hand each month before flash.
69:- Monthly roll of Texas transport usage tickets: Let Sitara transport usage tickets run for the whole contract term, take their rates from the rate matrix automatically, and carry last month's volumes forward.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets', which cites the same messages (1144, 1145, 1257, 1796, 2109, 2111, 867).
76:- Monthly Investor Relations volumetric explanations: Have the Statistical Database flag the +/-10% variances, show EOL and counterparty drivers, pre-fill last month's explanation, and collect the controllers' explanations in the database instead of by email.. Why: The change depends on things the mail does not show: that the Statistical Database holds EOL and counterparty detail, and that it does not already show the variances. The minutes are also inflated: 11 controllers' work is costed from one controller's two-line reply, and 11 readings are counted for a verifier who was copied only because one controller chose to copy him. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what the Statistical Database contains (variance columns, EOL or counterparty breakdowns), replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and other months' requests, and use them to show how long the explanations take and whether they repeat; then cost only the steps the change really removes.

26	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
27	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
28	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
29	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.

Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.

Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.

Proposal from analyst-3. Please check it against the corpus and save it or tell me what is wrong. (Nothing on liquidation support in decisions.md as of my last read; leads.md line 139 mentions it.)

TITLE: Have the risk system save each region's monthly liquidation detail (by category: price, basis, Gas Daily, capacity hedges and so on) to the ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations/<year>/<month> folder automatically at month close, instead of Jim Little requesting it region by region afterwards and desk analysts pulling it by hand

HOW IT WORKS TODAY / WHERE IT STALLS
For each flash month, Jim Little (liquidations accounting) needs support for the liquidation values each region booked. He emails the desk risk leads, often months later, listing the values per region and asking for the supporting detail. The risk lead (Giron) forwards the request to an analyst (Patrick Ryder), who pulls the deals and saves or emails them. Missing months are requested again in bulk.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/187.eml (Jim Little, 2/27/2001, to Phillip Love and Giron; Giron to Ryder: "Get this to Jim."): "Liqudation Flash Support for November 2000" / "I need support for: West  8,340,379 / Denver 2,441,357" / "Please let me know when this may be available.  You may save the support to ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations/\"year\"/\"month\"" / "I WILL ALSO NEED SUPPORT FOR THE  DECEMBER AND JANUARY VALUES FOR ALL OF YOUR REGIONS IF YOU HAVEN'T ALREADY SAVE THEM OUT TO THE ABOVE DIRECTORY."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/105.eml (Jim Little, 3/29/2001; Giron to Ryder: "Please get this info to Jim."): "In need liquidation support for the December Liquidation values below totalling 3,206,725." It includes a category breakdown (Price Positions 2,967,775; Basis Positions (17,255); Gas Daily Swaps 2,362; Capacity Hedges-Basis 253,843).
- corpus/giron-d/sent/163.eml (Giron to Little, 3/8/2001): "This file has the volumes for the liquidations."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
At month close, a scheduled report writes each region's liquidation detail, with the same category breakdown Jim uses, into the FRED Liquidations year/month folder he already names. Jim pulls the support himself, and the desks are asked only about exceptions.

AFTERWARDS
No request emails, no forwarding from risk leads to analysts, no hand-pulled deal lists, and no catch-up requests three months late for "DECEMBER AND JANUARY".

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly. Each flash month needs support per region, and the folder is organised by "year"/"month". The mail shows requests for Nov 2000, Dec 2000 and Jan 2001.
- Minutes per month today, West desk risk only (West and Denver regions): Jim's request and chasing ~10; Giron forwarding ~2; the analyst pulling and saving the supporting deals per region, ~20 × 2 regions = 40. Total ≈ 52 min.
- Afterwards: Jim opens the saved file himself ~5 min. Saved ≈ 47 min a month.
- 47 min ≈ 0.78 hours/month × $85 ≈ $67/month (≈ $800/yr). Phillip Love's regions in the same request (Sithe, Central) are not counted.

- corpus/giron-d/sent/163.eml (Giron to Little, 3/8/2001): "This file has the volumes for the liquidations."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
At month close, a scheduled report writes each region's liquidation detail, with the same category breakdown Jim uses, into the FRED Liquidations year/month folder he already names. Jim pulls the support himself, and the desks are asked only about exceptions.

AFTERWARDS
No request emails, no forwarding from risk leads to analysts, no hand-pulled deal lists, and no catch-up requests three months late for "DECEMBER AND JANUARY".

ESTIMATE
- Frequency: monthly. Each flash month needs support per region, and the folder is organised by "year"/"month". The mail shows requests for Nov 2000, Dec 2000 and Jan 2001.
- Minutes per month today, West desk risk only (West and Denver regions): Jim's request and chasing ~10; Giron forwarding ~2; the analyst pulling and saving the supporting deals per region, ~20 × 2 regions = 40. Total ≈ 52 min.
- Afterwards: Jim opens the saved file himself ~5 min. Saved ≈ 47 min a month.
- 47 min ≈ 0.78 hours/month × $85 ≈ $67/month (≈ $800/yr). Phillip Love's regions in the same request (Sithe, Central) are not counted.

I saw no text in these messages that tries to instruct an automated processor.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The problems are mostly in the evidence, and partly in the change itself.

**Already rejected once.** You may not have seen it, but `decisions.md` now has a rejection of this same work, "Monthly Investor Relations volumetric explanations". That version also proposed pre-filling last month's explanation and collecting the answers in the Statistical Database. Its reasons apply here too, and this version doesn't fix them.

**What the mail does support:**
- The request happens monthly. 1416.eml says Investor Relations wants "monthly volumetric analysis ... in addition to the quarterly analysis".
- The August request (1416.eml) went to 11 people.
- Baumbach (Texas) gave the same year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter drivers, EOL and Entex, for May (1210.eml) and August (1416.eml).

**What is wrong:**
1. **The cost of 11 controllers rests on one person's replies.** The only replies in the mail are Baumbach's: three lines in May and one line in August. Nothing shows how long the other 10 take, or whether their drivers repeat. "The answers repeat month to month" is shown for one region, two months apart, and only for the year and quarter comparisons. The month-to-month driver (TUFCO in May) isn't repeated in August.
2. **The minutes are too high.** The 15 minutes "today" against 5 minutes "after" assumes the review and the commercial check get shorter. Baumbach's August reply already reads like a quick confirmation. A tick in the database instead of a one-line email saves a minute or two per controller, not 10. The real saving is Misti Day no longer collecting and merging the emailed replies.
3. **The change drops a control the mail requires.** Misti writes: "It is essential that the volumes be verified by commercial personnel." That means checking the volumes, every month. The proposal limits it to "new or changed explanations", so it removes a required step and counts that as a saving.
4. **Smaller points.** The May request (1210.eml) went to Baumbach alone, not to 11 people. "June and September" are the reply dates; the data months were May and August.

**How to fix it:** Find replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and requests for other months, in mailboxes beyond farmer-d. Use them to show how long the explanations take and whether drivers repeat across regions. Then keep the monthly commercial check of volumes, and count only the steps the change really removes: the controllers' email replies and BA&R's consolidation. On current evidence that is probably well under an hour a month, not 125 minutes.
